signals.title: Anthropic offers Blackstone a 10%+ return on a ~$60B financing for ~1.5 GW of Google TPUs
signals.body: The FT reports Anthropic's "Project North Star" would fund Google TPU capacity with ~$42B of senior debt guaranteed by Broadcom and ~$18B of junior debt backed by its chip-lease payments, with Blackstone funds taking $9B. It is a huge order for the TPU supply chain, but a double-digit cost of capital echoes the AI-credit stress that hit CoreWeave last week. Terms are offers, not final.

links.why: Would guarantee the senior tranche and co-designs the TPUs being bought.
TPU vendor locking in a very large multi-year cloud customer.
Its funds would earn 10%+ on a $9B junior slice.
Manufactures the TPU chips.
If the best-funded AI lab pays 10%+, weaker neocloud borrowers face an even higher bar.

signals.title: Oct 21: Meta, Tesla, Texas Instruments, Lam Research and IBM report after the close
signals.body: The week's biggest AI-spending read: Meta's capex outlook will be judged against last week's AI-credit selloff, and Lam Research gives a read on chip-equipment orders after the chip index's 11% weekly fall. Tesla reports days after unveiling a redesigned Roadster (production targeted for 2028).

links.why: Its 2027 AI capex guide is the key number for the whole AI supply chain.
Reports after the Roadster unveil; robotaxi and energy-storage updates in focus.
Builds custom AI chips for Meta.
GPU supplier for Meta's AI clusters.

signals.title: Nasdaq -4.5% for the week, worst since June; chipmakers fall an 8th straight day (AMD -6%, Intel -5.8%, Micron -5.6%)
signals.body: Bloomberg data show chip stocks on their longest losing streak since 2008 as investors question whether AI infrastructure spending will earn its keep, especially when debt-funded. The S&P 500 fell 2% on the week while the Dow rose 0.7% as money rotated to energy and defensives. Intel reports Q3 on Oct 29, the next big test for the group.

links.why: Fell 6% on Oct 16; trades at ~48x forward earnings, so it is sensitive to any capex doubt.
Fell 5.8% to $89.85 ahead of Oct 29 results (guide up to $16.8B revenue).
Memory names lead the downside on pricing and China-supply worries.
Held up better (-1.4%) but sets the tone for the whole group.

signals.title: CoreWeave -12% to $61.39 (-25% on the week) as hedge funds dump AI names; Palantir -7.2% into a correction
signals.body: A Goldman note said hedge funds sold AI stocks at a fast pace in a "tactical rotation" away from smaller AI names, and AI software shed about $260B of value on Oct 16. CoreWeave hit its lowest level since its first year of trading as its bonds trade at distressed-looking levels. Debt-funded neoclouds are most exposed; cash-rich chip and platform leaders are less so.

links.why: Down 25% in a week; financing costs are now the story, not demand.
Fell 7.2% to $186 as AI software multiples compress.
Another leveraged GPU cloud that trades with CoreWeave.
Small-cap data-center landlord whose tenants rely on cheap debt.
CoreWeave is a big Nvidia buyer; funding stress could slow GPU orders at the margin.

signals.title: AI-infrastructure rout: chip index heads for 8th straight loss (longest since Oct 2008); Vertiv -6%, data-center suppliers lose ~$94B since Oct 6
signals.body: The PHLX Semiconductor Index was on track for its longest losing streak since October 2008 on Oct 15, and memory stocks fell for a fourth day. Six data-center equipment and construction firms, including Vertiv, GE Vernova and Eaton, have shed about $94B since Oct 6. CoreWeave bounced 5.9% to $69.69, but its credit default swaps imply about 60% odds of default within five years.

links.why: Down 6%+ on Oct 15; priced for uninterrupted data-center build-outs.
Bounced 5.9%, but CDS pricing still signals real credit stress.
Memory names have fallen four days running on hike fears and China DRAM supply.
The sector bellwether; -1.8% to $217.23 even as TSMC confirmed demand.

signals.title: Nasdaq futures +1.1% as AI and memory stocks bounce: Intel +4% on a JPMorgan upgrade, SanDisk +3.8%, Micron +2.7%
signals.body: After the Nasdaq's worst week since June (-4.5%) and an 11.4% weekly drop in the chip index, buyers returned pre-market Monday; JPMorgan lifted Intel to Neutral from Underweight ahead of its Oct 29 results. Memory names that fell 5-7% on Friday on AI-financing and China CXMT worries led the bounce. One morning's futures move does not settle the AI-credit debate; Meta and Tesla report Wednesday.

links.why: Upgraded to Neutral by JPMorgan; reports Q3 on Oct 29.
Memory leader bouncing after a 5-7% Friday drop.
Flash-storage name leading the pre-market rebound.
Neocloud up ~5% pre-market after last week's rout.
Up 1-3% pre-market after a 25% weekly fall; its ~15% bond yields remain the stress gauge.

signals.title: TSMC Q3: sixth straight record profit (+68.7%), FY26 growth lifted to ~44%, but gross margin dips to 66.4%
signals.body: TSMC beat estimates and guided Q4 revenue to $52.3B–$54.3B (~14% sequential growth at the midpoint), raising 2026 growth to about 44% from 40%. The stock still fell 2–4% on Oct 15 because gross margin slipped to 66.4% from 67.7% and the chip index was on its 8th straight down day. AI demand is intact; the selloff is about rates and valuation, not orders.

links.why: Record profit and a higher full-year guide; the dip is margin and macro, not demand.
Largest AI customer; TSMC guidance confirms Q4 wafer demand (NVDA closed -1.8% at $217.23).
Mid-cap materials supplier whose revenue tracks TSMC wafer starts.
Tool maker that benefits as TSMC keeps capex high for 2nm.

signals.title: Wolfspeed signs a multi-year 200mm silicon-carbide wafer supply deal with Infineon
signals.body: The deal replaces a 2024 agreement for smaller 150mm wafers; terms were not disclosed. It validates Wolfspeed's shift to 200mm wafers, with AI data-center power supplies joining EVs as demand drivers. Wolfspeed (~$1.2B market cap) carries a very high short float, so news like this can move it sharply both ways.

links.why: Volume validation for its 200mm wafers from one of the biggest power-chip buyers.
onsemi makes its own silicon carbide and competes for the same EV and data-center power sockets.

signals.title: BioXcel PDUFA date Nov 14 for IGALMI, but the company is in Chapter 11
signals.body: BioXcel filed for Chapter 11 on Aug 27, 2026, with Teva as stalking-horse bidder (~$57.5M upfront plus milestones, including the IGALMI sNDA). The Nov 14 date was set before the bankruptcy and no update was found, so this is not a normal binary catalyst for the stock.

signals.title: Nov 30: FDA decision on Cogent's bezuclastinib + sunitinib for GIST (priority review)
signals.body: The FDA accepted Cogent's application for bezuclastinib with sunitinib in previously treated gastrointestinal stromal tumors under priority review, with a decision listed for Nov 30. Approval would be Cogent's first product; analysts' average target is ~85% above the price. It is a mid cap, so the move would be smaller than a micro-cap binary.

links.why: First potential approval; cash ~$792M vs ~$309M yearly burn.
Pfizer sells sunitinib (Sutent), the backbone partner drug.

signals.title: Dec 17: FDA decision on Corcept's relacorilant resubmission (GRACE) for Cushing's syndrome
signals.body: Corcept resubmitted relacorilant after an earlier setback, and the FDA target date is Dec 17. The stock has nearly quadrupled from its 52-week low (now ~$110), so a lot of success is priced in. Approval would extend the franchise beyond its main drug Korlym.

links.why: Binary event on a stock that already ran ~280% off its low.

signals.title: Nov 14: FDA decision on Cytokinetics' aficamten (MAPLE-HCM data) in obstructive heart disease
signals.body: The FDA target date covers aficamten using MAPLE-HCM, the trial that compared it head-to-head with an older standard drug in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. A clean label would strengthen its case against Bristol Myers' Camzyos. Cytokinetics trades near $62, well under its $88 52-week high, with ~$1.2B of cash.

links.why: A label win would support the sales ramp; analysts' average target is ~$110.
Camzyos is the incumbent drug in the same disease.

signals.title: Oct 26: FDA decision on bepirovirsen for chronic hepatitis B
signals.body: The FDA is due to rule on bepirovirsen, the Ionis-discovered drug GSK is filing, which could be the first treatment aimed at a functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. One tracker puts approval odds near 85%. Approval would add a royalty stream for Ionis.

links.why: Discovered the drug and earns royalties if approved.
Licensee and seller; a needed new growth product.
Same-month FDA date (Oct 17) on its own presbyopia drop, partnered with Opus Genetics.

signals.title: Oct 24: Moderna investor webcast on Phase 3 melanoma cancer-vaccine data from ESMO
signals.body: Moderna and Merck will present late-breaking Phase 3 data on intismeran autogene, a personalized cancer vaccine given with Keytruda after melanoma surgery, in an ESMO 2026 Presidential Symposium, with an investor webcast on Oct 24. The stock has run to 52-week highs, joined the Nasdaq-100, and BofA lifted its target to $200 (Neutral), so expectations are high. A clear win could open a new cancer-vaccine market; anything less risks a sharp pullback.

links.why: The data decide whether Moderna becomes an oncology company; the stock already prices in a lot of success.
Co-develops the vaccine and shares its economics; it is given alongside Keytruda, extending that franchise.

signals.title: FDA expands ImmunityBio's Anktiva to papillary-only bladder cancer after an earlier refusal to file
signals.body: The Oct 14 approval covers BCG-unresponsive high-grade papillary NMIBC, based on a 62% complete response rate, roughly doubling Anktiva's addressable patients. Health care was the best S&P sector on the day (+2.4%). Rival bladder-cancer developers such as CG Oncology now face a broader incumbent.

links.why: Bigger label for its only product; 30% of the float is short.
Its cretostimogene targets the same patients; label breadth matters.
Keytruda is also approved in BCG-unresponsive bladder cancer.

signals.title: Labcorp to buy BioReference lab assets from OPKO for up to $872M; OPKO +12% to $1.53
signals.body: Labcorp will pay $722M at closing plus up to $150M tied to 4Kscore test revenue, subject to regulatory approval. OPKO jumped 12% to $1.53 as the sale turns a money-losing lab unit into cash. It is another step in the consolidation of US clinical labs, which favors the two giants.

links.why: Adds test volume at a modest price; fits its tuck-in strategy.
Small cap (~$1.1B) gets up to $872M, a large chunk of its market value, in cash.
Quest faces a bigger Labcorp in regional testing.

signals.title: Six Flags -14.4% to $10.20, near its 52-week low, after a rider dies on Goliath at Six Flags Over Georgia
signals.body: A guest died after falling from the Goliath coaster on Oct 12. The stock was already ~63% below its 52-week high on weak attendance and heavy debt, and now trades near 0.35x sales. Watch for ride closures, lawsuits and the Q3 attendance print.

links.why: A safety event on top of debt and attendance worries: very cheap but stressed, with 25% of the float short.

signals.title: Apple's $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo sells out of preorders within minutes ahead of its Oct 23 launch
signals.body: Some analysts read the sellout as supply limits rather than pure demand, but it was enough to make Apple the only Magnificent Seven stock up on Oct 16 (+0.4%). A strong foldable cycle helps Apple's average selling price and its component suppliers. It is a counterweight to earlier reports of iPhone 18 Pro order cuts.

links.why: A $1,999 device lifts average selling prices if supply catches up.
Radio-chip supplier hurt by earlier order-cut reports; a foldable hit helps.
Smaller Apple RF supplier with the same exposure.

signals.title: Barclays lifts Coca-Cola's target to $98 after KFC reportedly switches its fountain drinks to Coke from Pepsi
signals.body: The reported switch (Oct 15) is a share win for Coca-Cola at PepsiCo's expense; Pepsi trades near the bottom of its 52-week range while Coke sits near a high (~$94). Coca-Cola reports Q3 on Oct 27.

links.why: Wins a major restaurant account; reports Oct 27.
Loses a large fountain customer.

signals.title: Mortgage applications fall for a 6th straight week to the lowest since Jan 2025; 30-year rate ~7.5%
signals.body: MBA applications fell 2.7% in the week to Oct 9, with purchase and refinance both down, and the 30-year fixed rate sits near a three-year high. With CPI hot and October hike odds rising, relief looks far off. Homebuilders and mortgage lenders lose; renters' landlords gain pricing power.

links.why: Fewer applications mean fewer loans to originate.
Largest builder; leans on costly rate buydowns to sell homes.
Margins squeezed by incentives; analysts rate it Sell on average.
Entry-level buyers are the most rate-sensitive.

signals.title: Delta cuts 2026 EPS guide to $5.10–5.60 (was $6.50–7.50) on a ~$6B higher fuel bill
signals.body: Delta's Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.72 just missed the $1.76 estimate and Q3 fuel cost rose 62% to $4.1B. The CFO blamed the whole cut on fuel and sees jet fuel at $4.25/gal in Q4, while demand stays solid (Q4 revenue seen up ~20%, ~60% booked). Airlines stay a short-oil trade: they need Hormuz to reopen.

links.why: Guide cut entirely on fuel; demand is not the problem.
Weaker balance sheet and no refinery hedge, so fuel hurts more.
Refiners earn the jet and diesel margins airlines are paying.

signals.title: September retail sales +0.8% vs +0.3% expected, but ex-gas only +0.2%; retail ETF +3%, Nike and Lululemon +5%
signals.body: Sales beat forecasts and August was revised up to +1.3%, but gas stations alone rose 6.4%, so most of the beat is higher fuel bills. Excluding gas, sales rose just 0.2%, with restaurants (+1.1%) and department stores (+1.6%) still growing. Beaten-down retailers rallied on Oct 15 as yields fell.

links.why: Up ~5% on Oct 15 but still down ~42% this year; a bounce candidate if spending holds.
Up ~5%, trades at ~8x earnings after losing over half its value this year.
Gains share when gas eats household budgets.
Restaurant sales +1.1% support the group despite weak sentiment.

signals.title: SpaceX buys Grain's 800 MHz spectrum for ~$8B; AT&T -9.9%, Verizon -8.7%, T-Mobile -9.5%
signals.body: SpaceX agreed to buy a nationwide block of low-band spectrum (14 MHz paired) for about $8B in cash and says it will make Starlink 'a major mobile carrier'. The three US carriers lost roughly $50B+ in value in a day on fear of a new price-cutting rival; tower owner Crown Castle jumped 11% as a likely landlord. The deal still needs FCC approval.

links.why: Buyer; turns Starlink direct-to-phone into a full mobile network.
Most-traded stock Friday; a fourth national carrier would pressure pricing.
Same threat, with the weakest subscriber growth of the three.
The growth leader now faces a well-funded disruptor.
A new carrier needs towers; stock +11.3%.
Rival satellite-to-phone network; SpaceX now has its own spectrum.

signals.title: Michigan consumer sentiment falls to 46.3 in October (expected 47.6)
signals.body: Preliminary October sentiment dropped from 48.1 to 46.3, below forecasts, as cost-of-living frustration grows and consumers think the economy weakened this year. With fuel above $100 oil and mortgage rates near 7.5%, discretionary spenders and housing stay under pressure while discounters gain share.

links.why: Stretched shoppers trade down to the cheapest big-box option.
Weak confidence plus high rates keep first-time buyers away.
Already cut its outlook on fuel; softer demand would hurt fares.

signals.title: Bitcoin holds ~$82K and ether ~$2,436 as Fed officials cool October hike bets; spot ETFs still leak
signals.body: Bowman said the Fed has time to watch the economy after September's hike, and Daly said there is 'no urgency', pulling October hike odds to 32% from 54% (CME FedWatch). Bitcoin traded about $82,060 on Oct 16 after a $79.8K–$82.5K range, still about 35% below its $126K peak. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $261M on CPI day and have had outflows on five of the last seven days.

links.why: Trading volumes and staking revenue track price and sentiment.
Leveraged bitcoin proxy; most sensitive to a break of $80K.
IBIT flows are the clearest read on institutional demand.
Retail crypto trading rebounds if hike fears fade.

signals.title: Bitcoin slips to ~$81K and ether ~$2,360 as hot CPI revives hike bets
signals.body: Bitcoin lost $82,000 after core CPI beat forecasts and was near $81,040 early Oct 15, retesting the $80–82K support zone; analysts flag $75K if $80K breaks. Ether, XRP and Solana fell about 3%. Crypto brokers and treasury companies move with the tokens.

links.why: Trading volumes and fees track crypto prices.
Leveraged bitcoin holder.
Ether treasury company; value is mostly its ETH.
Crypto is a big swing factor in its revenue.

signals.title: Crypto ETFs flip to inflows: +$175.6M into bitcoin funds and +$24.8M into ether funds Oct 13
signals.body: The day's ~$199M net inflow interrupts an October outflow run that had pulled more than $1B from crypto ETFs. BTC holds near $83.4K and ETH near $2,500. One day is not a trend; today's CPI decides whether the bid lasts.

links.why: Custodian for most spot bitcoin ETFs; flows lift volumes.
IBIT is the largest bitcoin ETF; inflows add fees.
Leveraged bitcoin proxy; swings hardest on flow reversals.
Retail crypto trading volumes follow ETF sentiment.

signals.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs lose $82M and ether ETFs $70M on Oct 16, led by BlackRock; BTC holds ~$81.5K
signals.body: BlackRock's IBIT (-$71.8M) and ETHA (-$69.7M) accounted for nearly all the outflows, and bitcoin slipped below $81.5K as tech stocks sold off. Crypto is trading like a high-beta tech asset while hike odds stay high for December. Brokers and treasury-company stocks feel it first.

links.why: IBIT and ETHA led the redemptions.
Trading volumes fall when ETF demand fades.
Bitcoin treasury company with leveraged exposure.
Ether treasury company hit by ETHA outflows.

signals.title: Saylor hints at another Strategy bitcoin buy; BTC edges up to ~$82.8K
signals.body: Strategy holds 848,250 BTC at an average ~$75,444, so it is only ~10% in the money; last week it bought just 250 BTC while spending $192M repurchasing STRC preferred stock. Spot ETFs lost $82M (BTC) and $70M (ETH) on Oct 16, so corporate buyers are doing much of the lifting.

links.why: Largest corporate holder; buys depend on raising capital.
Trading and custody volumes rise with price.
Ether treasury company while ETH ETFs keep bleeding.

signals.title: SEC proposes wider crypto custody options for advisers; Coinbase merges US and Deribit derivatives
signals.body: The SEC proposed a rule giving registered advisers and funds clearer ways to hold crypto without always using a third-party custodian (now open for comment). Coinbase is relaunching a single regulated venue for US and international options and perpetuals with Deribit. Both make it easier for institutions to hold and hedge crypto.

links.why: Gains derivatives share and custody clients.
Fights for the same active-trader and advisor flows.
Institutional crypto services broaden with clearer rules.

signals.title: Leonardo DRS wins a spot on a $500M, 3-year counter-drone sensing IDIQ from JIATF-401
signals.body: DRS can now compete for task orders to supply expeditionary radars (from its RADA unit) for drone defense and short-range air defense. The ceiling is a maximum, not guaranteed revenue. Counter-drone demand is rising with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and US bases.

links.why: Mid-cap with ~52% upside to its average target; counter-drone radars are a growth line.
Also holds a JIATF-401 counter-UAS IDIQ; competes for the same task orders.
Small-cap counter-drone player chasing the same budgets.
Won $729M of LIDS counter-drone awards in the same week.

signals.title: Army awards $93.6M to nine firms, including General Dynamics, to build apps for its NGC2 battle network
signals.body: The one-year awards fund apps for the Next Generation Command and Control system, which runs on a data layer built by Anduril, Palantir, Raft and Striveworks. Most winners are private start-ups such as Onebrief and Rune Technologies. The platform owners gain the most, since every new app deepens their position.

links.why: General Dynamics Mission Systems is the only big listed winner.
Its data layer hosts the new apps.
Drone maker whose systems plug into such networks.

signals.title: Red Cat offers EUR 39 a share (~$230M) for Austria's Steyr Motors, a 28.9% premium; RCAT +5% pre-market
signals.body: The cash offer would bring Steyr's compact high-power engines in-house for Red Cat's Blue Ops uncrewed surface vessels; anchor holder B&C (~15%) has agreed to tender. It needs 50%+1 acceptance and approvals in Austria, Italy, Australia and the UK, with the acceptance period expected to end Dec 18. Red Cat withdrew an earlier proposal in July, and at ~$720M market cap this is a sizable bet for it.

links.why: Acquirer; vertical integration into maritime drone propulsion.
Unmanned-systems peer chasing the same naval drone budgets.
Larger drone maker; a reference for how the market values scale.

signals.title: Rocket Lab pushes Neutron debut to 2027; stock -10.9% and KeyBanc cuts its target to $100
signals.body: Rocket Lab delayed the first flight of its medium-lift Neutron rocket to next year, pushing the key test of its revenue story into 2027. Shares fell about 11% on Oct 15 to roughly $55, from ~$72 a week earlier. The delay leaves SpaceX's lead in medium-lift launch unchallenged for longer.

links.why: Neutron delay hits a stock priced at ~43x sales.
Less competition for national-security and constellation launches.
Satellite operators need more launch supply; delays keep prices high.

signals.title: Raytheon wins $729M of counter-drone deals (LIDS, KuRFS radar, Coyote) for the US Army, Qatar and Jordan
signals.body: The Oct 13 awards are the first international sales of the KuRFS radar and Coyote interceptor, and RTX is expanding Coyote production. Gulf demand for cheap drone defense is rising fast as Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia continue. Smaller counter-drone and drone-parts suppliers ride the same budget wave.

links.why: Adds to $30B+ of interceptor awards this month.
Leonardo DRS supplies counter-drone sensors and just won a spot on a $500M IDIQ.
Small-cap counter-drone (Iron Drone) maker that benefits from the same demand.
Sells drones and counter-drone systems to the Army.

signals.title: Raytheon wins a sole-source IDIQ with an $8B ceiling to modernize nuclear command-and-control (NC3) terminals
signals.body: The contract covers modernization, a production restart and studies for strategic communications terminals through 2036; only $0.8M was obligated at award, so revenue arrives slowly. It adds to Raytheon's $30.7B of interceptor awards earlier this month, ahead of RTX's Q3 results on Oct 20.

links.why: Sole-source winner; reports Oct 20 before the open.
Prime on the Sentinel ICBM, part of the same nuclear-modernization push; also reports Oct 20.
Competes in military communications and terminals.

signals.title: Raytheon lands $30.7B of interceptor deals: up to $24.4B for SM-6 and $6.3B for SM-3 Block IB
signals.body: The Navy and Missile Defense Agency signed five-year deals (extendable to seven) to push SM-6 output above 500 a year, under February frameworks that aim to double to quadruple munitions production. Gulf missile attacks are draining interceptor stocks. Suppliers of rocket motors, seekers and electronics also benefit.

links.why: Prime contractor; multi-year visibility on its best-selling missiles.
Supplies SM-3 rocket-motor stages.
Aerojet Rocketdyne unit makes missile rocket motors.
Mid-cap maker of missile electronics and processing boards.

signals.title: Ukraine fires ~1,015 drones at Russia, hitting a St. Petersburg oil terminal, after Trump waives new Russia sanctions
signals.body: Russia's defense ministry counted about 1,015 drones on Oct 18; Zelensky said Russia launched ~2,700 drones and 66 missiles at Ukraine over the past week. Mass drone warfare keeps demand high for cheap drones, counter-drone systems and interceptors, and the oil-terminal strike adds to supply risk.

links.why: Loitering-munition and drone demand.
US-made drone components supplier (small cap).
Counter-drone sensors.
Air-defense interceptors used against missile and drone salvos.

signals.title: Borr Drilling director Tor Olav Trøim lifts his stake to 12.2% with ~10M shares of open-market buys
signals.body: A 13D filed Oct 13 shows Trøim bought about 10 million shares between Aug 13 and Oct 9, the largest block on Oct 9 at $4.74, and he kept buying on Oct 13–14. Borr is a ~$1.4B jackup driller with $2.5B of debt, so it is a leveraged bet on oil staying above $100. Shares have risen ~72% in a year.

links.why: Insider with a long record in offshore (Seadrill, Golar) buying heavily; debt is the risk.
Larger offshore driller; already trades above its average target.
High oil prices that justify the rig demand also lift producers.

signals.title: Brent touches $110 and settles at $109.86 (+3.7%), a 5-month high; WTI $101.41, up 10%+ on the week
signals.body: Iran escalated attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthis fired more missiles at Saudi Arabia and Ukraine vowed to keep hitting Russian refineries. Energy led the S&P 500 on Oct 16 (Exxon and Chevron +2.5%, Permian Resources +4.2% on a Scotiabank upgrade). Airlines and other fuel users lose as triple-digit crude also feeds inflation worries before the Fed.

links.why: Mid-cap Permian producer at ~10x forward earnings and ~5.5x EBITDA; upgraded to Outperform.
Higher-beta US producer with more upside to $100+ oil.
Tanker rates jump when Gulf routes are disrupted.
Diesel cracks stay wide as Ukraine targets Russian refineries.
Already cut 2026 guidance on fuel; $110 Brent adds pressure.

signals.title: Two ships sink near Hormuz after projectile strikes; Brent ~$104 as the US weighs easing tanker sanctions
signals.body: A container ship and a bulk carrier sank within 24 hours near the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent settled at $106.06 on Oct 14 before easing to ~$104.40 on reports the US may let sanctioned "shadow fleet" tankers carry oil again. API data showed an 11.1M-barrel US crude draw. Relief for sanctioned ships would add tanker supply and could cool record freight rates.

links.why: Freed shadow-fleet tankers would add supply and pressure rates.
Mid-cap VLCC owner; trades at its analyst target already.
Small-cap tanker owner; above its analyst target.
Oil producer gains while Brent stays above $100.
Refiner; a big crude draw supports margins.

signals.title: IEA speeds up emergency stock release, including 20M+ barrels of diesel; US weighs easing shadow-fleet sanctions; Brent ~$105.5
signals.body: IEA members agreed Oct 15 to release over 20 million barrels of diesel plus the rest of the March emergency release. Washington is also considering lifting sanctions on some shadow-fleet tankers to cut record freight rates. Brent slipped to $105.51 and WTI to $97.43 early Oct 16, but traders called the steps too small while Houthi-Saudi attacks escalate.

links.why: Released diesel could narrow record refining margins.
Freeing shadow-fleet ships adds supply to a tight tanker market.
VLCC rates near records could ease if sanctioned tankers return.
Mid-size tanker owner; same freight-rate risk.
Cheaper jet fuel and diesel would ease airline costs.

signals.title: Next OPEC+ monthly review: Nov 1
signals.body: The group will also start assessing capacity for 2027 quotas.

signals.title: Oil eases ~1% as a Russian diesel deal offsets Houthi threats; OPEC cuts 2026 demand growth to 400K bpd
signals.body: Brent fell $1.30 to about $105.35 and WTI to about $92.49 early Oct 13 after the US temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel so Russia can supply diesel to world markets, though lawmakers from both parties are questioning the deal. Gulf risk still dominates: the Houthis hit Riyadh's airport, tankers were attacked near Hormuz, and OPEC and non-OPEC ministers say shipping and insurance costs now top a third of the oil's value. OPEC has cut its 2026 demand-growth forecast to 400,000 bpd from 1.4 million at the start of the year.

links.why: More Russian diesel on the water would narrow the unusually fat diesel margins US refiners are earning.
Every dollar off fuel helps an airline that just cut guidance on a ~$6B higher fuel bill.
Record freight and insurance costs are tanker owners' revenue.
Mid-cap VLCC owner earning record spot rates on Gulf voyages.
Upstream producer whose cash flow tracks Brent; a de-escalation would hit it first.

signals.title: Brent slips ~1.8% to ~$108 after Trump waives new Russia sanctions and tariffs on buyers of Russian oil
signals.body: Trump's Oct 16 order lifts the newest package while older sanctions stay, and Rubio said assessing the effects could take up to 60 days. Supply risk has not gone away: Ukraine hit a St. Petersburg terminal, two tankers were attacked off Saudi Arabia, and Morgan Stanley raised its Q4 Brent forecast to $105. Producers give back part of last week's jump; refiners and airlines get some relief.

links.why: High-beta US producer that rallied with crude.
Permian producer; earnings track WTI.
Cheaper crude input if product margins hold.
Fuel is its biggest swing cost after a guidance cut.

signals.title: VLCC rates ease to ~$800K/day (-8.6% w/w) from records while product-tanker rates jump ~40%
signals.body: Crude-tanker earnings stay extraordinary even after the dip, as Gulf disruption reroutes cargoes, while LR1/LR2 product tankers surge on the IEA diesel release and refinery dislocations. Washington is weighing easing shadow-fleet sanctions to cool freight costs, a risk to rates.

links.why: VLCC-heavy fleet earning near-record spot rates.
Pure VLCC spot exposure.
Mid-size crude and product tankers benefit from the product-rate jump.

signals.title: Bank of America profit -17% on a $1.2B AML penalty (stock -4.7%); Morgan Stanley beats; BlackRock AUM hits $15.5T
signals.body: BofA earned $0.91 a share, missing forecasts, as a $1.2B Treasury penalty and softer trading hit results. Morgan Stanley beat ($3.03 vs $2.91, revenue $20.34B) on banking and equities, and BlackRock pulled in $205B of new money. Trading-heavy firms are winning this quarter; lenders with regulatory baggage are lagging.

links.why: Penalty is one-off, but revenue also missed.
Beat on deals and equities; wealth unit steadies earnings.
Record $15.5T AUM; ETF inflows of $135B.
Last week's blowout trading quarter sets the bar.

signals.title: Regional and custody banks beat: Schwab record $7.2B revenue (adj. EPS $1.69, +29%), U.S. Bancorp and PNC top estimates, BNY +20% profit
signals.body: Schwab client assets reached $13.3T, and U.S. Bancorp posted record net revenue of $7.97B. PNC beat on earnings ($5.09 vs $4.89) but missed slightly on revenue, and BNY earned $2.37 a share vs $2.26 expected. Strong markets and fees are offsetting worries about rates and credit.

links.why: Record quarter; trading and cash balances both strong.
Record revenue; trades ~10x forward earnings with a 3.8% yield.
EPS beat; ~24% upside to the average target.
Custody fees ride high asset prices.

signals.title: Brazil runoff tightens: CNT/MDA has Flávio Bolsonaro 46.8% vs Lula 45.9%; Datafolha lead narrows to 47–45
signals.body: Three polls released Oct 15–16 all fall within the margin of error, so the Oct 25 runoff is a toss-up even though prediction markets have favoured Flávio. A Bolsonaro win is widely seen as market-friendly for Brazilian banks and Petrobras; a Lula upset could hit them. Expect volatility in Brazilian ADRs into the vote.

links.why: Nubank has the most retail exposure to Brazil sentiment.
Brokerage flows rise when local markets rally.
Largest private bank; moves with the real and political risk.
Petrobras policy (pricing, dividends) is the biggest election swing factor.
Small-cap payments name with high beta to Brazil rates.

signals.title: Brazil runoff: two new polls show a tie (BTG/Nexus Flavio 50.3-49.7; Vox Lula 51-49) while Polymarket moves to 81% Flavio
signals.body: Valid-vote polls taken Oct 15-18 are inside the margin of error, yet prediction-market money (~$187M traded) leans further toward Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of the Oct 25 vote. Investors broadly see a Flavio win as friendlier for Brazilian banks and Petrobras; a Lula upset would likely hit the real and state-linked stocks.

links.why: State-controlled oil major; policy and dividend outlook hinge on the winner.
Largest private bank; moves with the real and rates.
Digital bank with most of its customers in Brazil.
Brokerage whose flows track local market sentiment.
Small-business payments; sensitive to Brazilian rates.

signals.title: September CPI runs hot: 3.7% y/y (est. 3.6%), core +0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y; S&P -1.1%, 10Y ~5.28%
signals.body: Gasoline jumped 9.1% in the month and drove more than half of the 0.6% headline rise; shelter, airfares and used cars pushed core above forecasts. The Nasdaq fell 1.9% and the Russell 2000 1.9%, while the Dow held flat thanks to health care. Rate-sensitive stocks lose; energy producers and defensives held up.

links.why: Mortgage lender; higher yields keep refinancing dead.
Homebuilder demand falls as 30-year mortgages sit near 7.5%.
Higher rates lift its cash yields but push clients to money funds.
Small bank with deposit costs tied to rates.

signals.title: Fed hold odds for Oct 28 rise to ~85% as the 10Y eases to ~5.06%; Bessent calls inflation an "energy shock"
signals.body: CME FedWatch puts an October hike at ~15% (Polymarket "no change" 87%), and the Fed is in its blackout until the meeting. Treasury Secretary Bessent said September's hot CPI reflects the Iran-conflict energy spike and should ease. Lower hike odds help homebuilders and lenders; NAHB (today) and housing starts (Tuesday) are the next tests.

links.why: Largest homebuilder; mortgage rates drive orders.
Homebuilder leaning on rate buydowns.
Mortgage lender; volumes jump when yields fall.
Earns on client cash; rate path matters.

signals.title: October hike odds fall to 17% (from 28%), December stays ~89%; Warsh gives no signal and the 10Y ends near 5.10%
signals.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said at an IMF event in Bangkok "it's a new chapter at the Fed," without hinting at the Oct 27–28 decision. Traders now mostly expect a December hike instead of October after hot CPI and PPI. Rate-sensitive housing and lenders get a short reprieve, but $110 oil keeps inflation risk alive.

links.why: Mortgage volumes depend on rates falling, and a December hike is still priced.
Builders need lower mortgage rates to lift demand.
Higher-for-longer rates support its net interest income.
Small bank whose funding costs track Fed moves.

signals.title: Sept PPI +1.3% (largest since 2022), yet 10Y falls 10bp to ~5.09% as Fed officials talk down an October hike; odds drop to 32%
signals.body: Producer prices jumped 1.3% in September and 6.3% from a year earlier, well above the 0.6% monthly forecast. Bonds rallied anyway after Bowman and Daly signaled no rush, cutting October hike odds to 32% from 54%; a December hike is still priced at ~90%. The 30-year fell ~10bp to 5.43%, its best day since Nov 2024, and Lennar rose 5%.

links.why: Up 5% as long yields fell; still down ~25% this year.
Builder margins depend on mortgage rates near 7.5%.
Mortgage volumes need yields to keep falling.
Higher-for-longer rates support its cash spreads.

signals.title: Alcoa beats: Q3 adjusted EPS $1.82 vs $1.49 expected, free cash flow $472M; stock up ~5.8% on Oct 16
signals.body: Higher alumina output and lower capex drove the free-cash-flow jump, though revenue ($3.70B) was a touch light and Q4 has ~$60M of aluminum-segment headwinds. Alcoa trades at ~7x earnings and ~3.5x EBITDA. Its pending ~$3.1B purchase of South32 assets is on track for H1 2027.

links.why: Cheap on earnings with a fresh beat; aluminum prices are the swing factor.
Century Aluminum, a smaller US smelter at ~5.7x earnings, trades on the same metal price.

signals.title: China Q3 GDP +4.5% beats (4.4% expected); LME copper rises 0.5% to $14,498/t
signals.body: September industrial output grew 5.5% and retail sales 1.1% (0.6% expected), easing fears about the biggest metals buyer. Copper recovers above last week's $14,338 low, while gold holds ~$4,180 and silver ~$57.60 as hike bets fade.

links.why: Largest US-listed copper producer.
Low-cost copper miner with long reserves.
Copper-focused after selling its coal unit.
Mid-cap copper producer with high leverage to price.
Small/mid-cap Brazilian copper miner.

signals.title: Copper holds ~$6.6/lb despite a firmer dollar; Polymarket gives 35% odds of US copper-cable tariffs by year-end
signals.body: COMEX copper edged up on Oct 12 even as the dollar index rose to 102.57, while Freeport (-0.5%) and Southern Copper (-0.3%) slipped. Talks at Antofagasta's Centinela mine, on strike since Oct 7, had not resumed as of Oct 9. Polymarket prices 35% odds of Section 232 tariffs on copper cable by Dec 31, 2026 and 46.5% by end-2027; a tariff would widen the US premium over LME prices.

links.why: Largest US copper producer (Morenci); a US tariff would lift what its domestic copper sells for.
Mid-cap Brazil producer with rising output; leveraged to a tight market.
Mid-cap with Arizona (Copper World) growth plans that a US premium would help.
Large Chilean exposure (QB2); benefits from high prices but faces the same Chilean labour risks.

signals.title: Gold recovers to ~$4,196 while LME copper drops a 3rd day to $14,338/t; AngloGold +3.5% on a Goldman Buy
signals.body: Gold rose ~0.6% on Oct 15 as yields fell, and silver bounced 1.6% after its 6% CPI-day plunge. Copper slid 1.1% on hike fears even with the Centinela strike. Goldman started AngloGold Ashanti at Buy with a $104 target.

links.why: New Goldman Buy; ~10x forward earnings with a ~3.9% yield.
Largest gold miner; tracks bullion.
Copper price slide hits the biggest US copper producer.
Small/mid-cap copper miner with high copper beta.

signals.title: Gold edges up to ~$4,182 and copper holds ~$6.61/lb, but miners slide (FCX -1.2%) ahead of CPI
signals.body: Gold stabilized after its 2-month low while copper miners fell more than the metal despite a weaker dollar (DXY -0.36%). Polymarket prices 36% odds of US copper-cable tariffs by year-end. A hot CPI would lift yields and pressure non-yielding gold.

links.why: Benchmark copper miner; fell 1.2% to $72.42.
Trades ~18% above its average target with a Sell consensus; a crowded copper trade.
Largest gold miner, 33% net margin at ~13x forward earnings.

signals.title: Jan 10, 2027: US–China rare-earth truce now expires; stocks slide a 2nd day (USAR -5%)
signals.body: The Busan truce on China's rare-earth export controls was extended from Nov 10 to Jan 10, 2027 (Bessent, Sep 23), so the near-term supply scare has faded. USAR fell another 5% to $12.58 on Oct 8 and is down 29% in a month. MP has held up best because it already has sales.

links.why: US magnet champion with a DoD price floor; trades on China headlines.
Small-cap US magnet developer, fell 5% Oct 7.
Small-cap rare-earth developer, fell 3%.
Auto magnet supply is exposed if China reimposes controls.

signals.title: Silver plunges 6.3% to ~$55.77 and gold settles -1.7% at $4,107.90 after hot CPI; copper -1.9% to $6.60/lb
signals.body: October hike odds jumped and the dollar firmed, knocking precious metals back toward last week's two-month lows. Silver miners carry the most leverage to the move. Copper also slipped despite tight Chilean supply.

links.why: Silver-heavy miner; most exposed to the drop.
Largest US silver producer.
Gold major; earnings track the gold price.
Copper slipped, but Chile supply stays tight.

signals.title: Agios: FDA decision Nov 1 on sickle cell, with ~$930M of net cash against a $1.8B market cap
signals.body: Agios already sells mitapivat for two rare anemias, and the FDA is reviewing it for sickle cell disease under priority review (accelerated approval). Phase 3 hit on hemoglobin but missed on pain crises, which halved the stock in Nov 2025, so approval odds and label scope are the debate. Analysts' $46 average target is ~50% above the price; risk: a rejection or narrow label, and a ~$365M yearly cash burn.

links.why: A cash-backed shot at a large new market; the mixed Phase 3 is why it's cheap.

signals.title: Annexon: Phase 3 blindness readout plus a second drug filing
signals.body: Two shots on goal: GA Phase 3 in Q4 plus a GBS approval path (EU review, US filing). Target ~3.7x price. Risk: Geographic atrophy has a history of failed trials; ~$190M yearly burn means dilution if data disappoints.

links.why: The largest potential payoff in the Moonshots, but also the hardest trial to win.

signals.title: Byrna Technologies: a ~$113M maker of non-lethal launchers, down ~80% in a year, with six insiders buying and no debt
signals.body: Sales fell 46% last quarter as e-commerce and dealer reorders slumped, but Byrna has no debt, still made slightly positive free cash flow over the last year and keeps mid-60s% gross margins. Six insiders bought about $400K of stock in filings through Oct 16. Risk: cash is only ~$9.4M, the turnaround depends on holiday sales and new retail doors in early 2027, and further declines would pressure the balance sheet.

links.why: A deep-value turnaround bet: at ~1.2x sales the stock prices in decline, so any sales stabilization could re-rate it sharply.

signals.title: Capricor: DMD cell-therapy FDA decision Nov 22, target ~3.5x the price
signals.body: Capricor's deramiocel hit its Phase 3 primary endpoint (upper-limb function in Duchenne) and the FDA review was extended to Nov 22 after new 24-month data. The stock is $7.75 vs a $27 average target, with ~$238M cash. Risk: it already got one rejection in 2025, 34% of the float is short, and a second 'no' could halve it.

links.why: A true binary: approval could re-rate it several-fold, a rejection could cut it in half.

signals.title: Nov 1: FDA decision on Agios' mitapivat for sickle cell disease
signals.body: Priority-review sNDA under the accelerated approval pathway, based on the RISE UP Phase 3 hemoglobin-response result. Approval would add the largest market yet for a drug Agios already sells.

links.why: Binary event: label scope matters as much as approval.

signals.title: Q4: Annexon ARCHER II Phase 3 topline
signals.body: Phase 3 ARCHER II topline for vonaprument in geographic atrophy (a cause of blindness). Company guides runway into 2H 2027 (~$209M cash).

links.why: Binary event: the stock can move 50%+ either way.

signals.title: Nov 22: FDA decision on Capricor deramiocel (Duchenne)
signals.body: PDUFA goal date after a 3-month extension for a major amendment. Indication narrowed to upper-limb function, the trial's primary endpoint.

links.why: Binary FDA decision.

signals.title: Q4: Helus Phase 3 APPROACH topline (HLP003 in depression)
signals.body: Enrollment finished Aug 14; the company guides to topline data in Q4 2026, exact date TBA. This is the main value driver for the stock.

links.why: Binary readout.

signals.title: Oct 30: FDA decision on INOVIO's INO-3107
signals.body: FDA decision on INO-3107 (accelerated approval) for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. About $37M cash (incl. a July raise) and ~$18M/quarter burn; company guides runway into late Q1 2027.

links.why: Binary event: the stock can move 50%+ either way.

signals.title: Dec 22: FDA decision on Mineralys' lorundrostat for hypertension
signals.body: PDUFA date for lorundrostat in combination with other blood-pressure drugs. Cash is guided to fund the launch into 2028.

links.why: Binary event: approval opens a large market; a delay would hit a single-asset company hard.

signals.title: Nov 28: FDA decision on PolyPid's D-PLEX100 (surgical-site infection prevention)
signals.body: Priority review; the NDA was accepted Jul 27. A binary event for a ~$97M company: approval triggers Azurity milestones, a rejection likely means dilution.

links.why: Most of the value rides on this decision.

signals.title: Late Nov: Sol-Gel Phase 3 patidegib topline
signals.body: Phase 3 topline for SGT-610 (patidegib gel) in Gorlin syndrome. ~$48M cash vs ~$9M yearly burn: several years.

links.why: Binary event: the stock can move 50%+ either way.

signals.title: Nov 22: FDA decision on Savara's MOLBREEVI (autoimmune PAP)
signals.body: PDUFA goal date for Savara's inhaled GM-CSF. UK decision is expected in Q4 and EU in Q1 2027. Approval would unlock up to ~$150M of non-dilutive capital, per the company.

links.why: First product; binary outcome.

signals.title: Dec 12: FDA decision on Vanda's Quimilza (imsidolimab) for generalized pustular psoriasis
signals.body: The FDA decision date for Vanda's imsidolimab license application is Dec 12, 2026, per the company's Q2 release. Approval adds a rare-disease product to a company trading near its cash; a rejection would leave it reliant on Fanapt and the BYSANTI launch.

links.why: Binary event for a ~$270M company.
Originator of imsidolimab.

signals.title: Sprinklr: a $1.36B software company with $453M cash, $128M free cash flow and a director buying $850K
signals.body: Sprinklr sells customer-experience software to large companies; revenue is flat (~$873M), but it generates ~9% free-cash-flow yield and has cut its share count ~8% in a year. Director Stephen Ward bought 150,000 shares at $5.67 on Oct 13, and the average target (~$8.4) is ~44% above the price. Risk: no growth means no re-rating, and AI could shrink seat-based contact-center software.

links.why: A steadier Moonshot: cash is a third of the market cap and buybacks are running; the bet is on growth returning or a buyer showing up.
Another cheap, slow-growth software small cap; shows how the market prices no-growth SaaS.

signals.title: Helus sets an Oct 21 investor event on its Phase 3 depression drug; stock -6.5% to $11.03
signals.body: Helus Pharma will webcast an Oct 21 presentation on HLP003 (Phase 3, add-on treatment for major depression) and HLP004 (Phase 2, anxiety) with outside experts. The release gave no new timing for the APPROACH Phase 3 topline, which is still guided to Q4 2026. Shares fell 6.5% on Oct 12 as volatility builds into the binary readout.

links.why: Expect volatility around the event; the Phase 3 readout is what matters.
Psychedelic-medicine peer; a Helus win or loss moves sentiment across the group.

signals.title: Helus Pharma: Phase 3 depression readout in Q4, insiders just bought $6.3M
signals.body: Helus (formerly Cybin) finished enrolling its Phase 3 APPROACH trial of psychedelic-derived HLP003 for depression and expects topline data in Q4 2026. Four insiders bought ~$6.3M of stock near $12.58 on Oct 1, and analysts' average target is ~3.5x the price. Risk: share count doubled in a year, it burns ~$140M a year, and a Phase 3 miss would likely cut the stock by more than half.

links.why: Binary but well-funded: insiders buying right before data is a meaningful signal.
Compass Pathways' psilocybin Phase 3 sets the bar for the field.

signals.title: INOVIO: $120M company, one FDA decision away from its first product
signals.body: Late-cycle FDA meeting and inspections are done; Breakthrough and Orphan status; an approval would be its first product, at a ~$120M valuation. Risk: Share count nearly doubled in a year; even with approval it will likely need to raise money again in early 2027.

links.why: Classic binary setup: one FDA decision on Oct 30 decides most of the value. Size it so a zero is survivable.

signals.title: Mineralys: blood-pressure drug up for FDA approval Dec 22, cash ~1/3 of market cap
signals.body: Lorundrostat lowers aldosterone for hard-to-control hypertension and has a 1,083-patient Phase 3 behind it; the FDA decision is Dec 22. Mineralys holds ~$661M of cash, bought out its royalty to Tanabe, and analysts' target (~$48.50) is about twice the price after a 50% fall from the high. Risk: one-drug company, AstraZeneca has a rival drug in the same class, and launch costs mean more burn.

links.why: A late-stage, well-funded approval bet: risk 3, not a lottery ticket, but still binary.
Developing baxdrostat, a rival aldosterone-synthase drug.

signals.title: Immersion leaves the Moonshots to make room for PolyPid
signals.body: Immersion had no dated catalyst and the list was over its 12-pick limit; it rotates out at $6.96 (Oct 16 close), still cheap on cash flow but carrying ~$273M of debt against ~$210M of cash. PolyPid adds a dated FDA decision (Nov 28) with a commercial partner already signed.

links.why: New pick: binary FDA decision Nov 28.
Removed; still a cash-flow story, but no near-term catalyst.

signals.title: Opus Genetics wins FDA approval of RYZUMVI for presbyopia, but the stock falls 5.2% to $3.84 and leaves the Moonshots
signals.body: The FDA approved phentolamine 0.75% drops (RYZUMVI) for age-related near-vision loss; partner Viatris will sell it in the US and Opus gets an undisclosed milestone. Investors sold the news, as presbyopia drops have launched slowly before. With the binary event resolved, the pick leaves the Moonshots; the next questions are launch timing and sales.

links.why: Approval done; the stock now depends on Viatris's launch and milestone payments.
Viatris holds US rights and will run the launch.

signals.title: Vanda's social-anxiety drug VQW-765 fails Phase 3; stock sits at its 52-week low (~$4.04)
signals.body: The Oct 14 miss pauses that program, but the main reason Vanda is a Moonshot, the Dec 12 FDA decision on imsidolimab for generalized pustular psoriasis, is unchanged. With ~$170M of cash against a ~$244M market cap and heavy cash burn, the pick now rests on that one decision.

links.why: Pipeline setback, but cash is ~70% of market cap and the Dec 12 decision is intact.

signals.title: PolyPid: ~$97M company with an FDA decision Nov 28 and a partner already signed
signals.body: D-PLEX100, a local slow-release antibiotic that aims to prevent surgical-site infections after colorectal surgery, has priority review with a Nov 28 FDA date, and Azurity has licensed it in a deal worth up to ~$320M. Risk: June 30 cash was only $6.6M, so the runway into 2028 depends on Azurity milestones, and a rejection would likely force a dilutive raise.

links.why: Binary but partner-funded: approval brings milestones and royalties on a ~$97M market cap; a rejection could cut it in half or worse.

signals.title: Sol-Gel: insiders own 60%, Phase 3 readout late November
signals.body: Insiders own ~60%, cash covers years of spending, and there are no approved drugs for this condition. Breakthrough and Orphan designations. Risk: One trial decides it; a miss could cut the stock in half or worse. Small float means big swings.

links.why: The rare small cap where insiders own most of it and there's no near-term need to raise money. That's what makes it stand out.

signals.title: Savara: first-ever drug for a rare lung disease up for FDA approval Nov 22
signals.body: Savara's inhaled molgramostim for autoimmune PAP, a disease with no approved drug, has a Nov 22 FDA date; JPMorgan just started at Overweight ($12) and the average target is ~$10.94 vs $4.88. Short interest is ~34% of float, so an approval could force a squeeze. Risk: a rejection or another delay would hit hard, and it burns ~$110M a year.

links.why: A clean binary: approval makes it a commercial orphan-drug company; a rejection likely means dilution.
Insmed's Arikayce shows how valuable an inhaled rare-lung drug can be.
Rare-lung inhaled franchise and a possible acquirer type.

signals.title: Unusual Machines: maker of US-built drone parts, with ~$316M cash, about 30% of its ~$1B market cap
signals.body: The Orlando company sells motors, cameras and other components to US drone builders, a niche that Pentagon 'buy American' drone rules favor. ProPublica reported Oct 9 that the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital weighed a $220M loan to it, amid conflict-of-interest scrutiny of the official involved. Analysts' $39 target is ~1.9x the price. Risk: ~33x sales on $32M of revenue, still loss-making, and the share count nearly tripled in a year.

links.why: A policy-driven growth story with plenty of cash; the price already assumes a lot of growth.
Drone systems peer at ~22x sales with 43% of its float short.
US military drone maker, the kind of buyer that needs non-Chinese components.

signals.title: Vanda: ~$270M company with ~$170M cash, $216M sales, and an FDA decision Dec 12
signals.body: The market values Vanda at about 1.3x sales and book even though it sells several approved drugs, has a new schizophrenia drug launching and has an FDA decision on Quimilza (imsidolimab, for a rare psoriasis) due Dec 12. Analysts' target is ~2.6x the price. Risk: Losses are heavy (~$143M yearly cash burn) as HETLIOZ sales collapse to generics, and Vanda has a long, combative history with the FDA. Update Oct 14: its social-anxiety drug VQW-765 failed Phase 3; the Dec 12 imsidolimab decision is unchanged.

links.why: Cash covers most of the market cap, so you pay little for the pipeline. The launch and the Dec 12 decision decide whether the burn slows.
AnaptysBio originated imsidolimab and is listed on the same Dec 12 decision.

signals.title: Anthropic IPO: public S-1 expected in late October (date TBA); roadshow week of Nov 9, trading targeted before Nov 26
signals.body: No public S-1 had appeared by Oct 19; the SEC's 15-day rule implies one by about Oct 23-25 if the roadshow starts the week of Nov 9 (Bloomberg). Valuation talk is $1.8-2T vs a $965B private round in May, with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan reported as bookrunners. The earlier reported Oct 26 filing date is not confirmed.

links.why: Listed fund holding late-stage private tech; IPOs set marks for its holdings.
Joint bookrunner.
Joint bookrunner.

signals.title: SpaceX lockup for pre-IPO holders ends around Dec 9 (estimated from its 180-day term)
signals.body: SpaceX listed Jun 12 at $135 (about a $1.77T valuation) and peaked at $211, then fell to around $123-125 by late July. Staggered 180-day lockups for non-insider pre-IPO holders end around Dec 9, while insider lockups run 366 days. Supply from VC and growth funds could weigh on the stock and on marks for listed private-tech vehicles.

links.why: Early investors can sell after the lockup ends; supply can weigh on the stock.
Holds pre-IPO stakes, so its value tracks how listings trade.
Listed launch peer that trades with SpaceX sentiment.

signals.title: EMK closes a EUR 1.25B (~$1.4B) continuation fund for Dutch installer VDK Groep, led by LGT and Coller
signals.body: GP-led continuation funds keep standing in for classic exits while sale and IPO windows stay narrow; separately, Apax is buying Warburg Pincus's stake in Dutch telco Odido to take full control. Secondaries buyers earn discounts and fees, and existing investors get liquidity without a sale.

links.why: Runs one of the largest secondaries businesses (Strategic Partners).
Uses continuation vehicles and secondaries for its own exits.
Smaller listed secondaries and co-invest platform.

signals.title: CCC signs a $7.75/share, $6.1B take-private with GTCR and Elliott: 44% premium, about 19x EBITDA
signals.body: The all-cash deal is 44% above CCC's unaffected July 9 close and 59% above its 30-day average; it closed at $7.63 on Oct 15, just below the offer. It values the insurance-claims software firm at about 19x trailing EBITDA of ~$318M. J.P. Morgan and Citi committed financing, and closing is expected in Q1 2027 after a shareholder vote.

links.why: Now a merger-arbitrage stock: ~1.6% gross spread to $7.75 into a Q1 2027 close.
Sponsor-led take-privates of mid-cap software are back, which supports alternative managers' deal fees.

signals.title: Ramp raises $1.85B at a $60B valuation, led by Dragoneer
signals.body: One of the year's largest fintech rounds marks Ramp's corporate-card and spend-software business far above listed peers' multiples. It shows late-stage money is still chasing AI-flavored fintech and gives secondary buyers a fresh mark.

links.why: Spend and payables rival trading at ~2.4x sales, a fraction of Ramp's private multiple.
Corporate-card incumbent Ramp is taking share from.
Listed fund of late-stage private tech; big private marks tend to support sentiment for such vehicles.

AA.name: Alcoa
AA.about: Aluminum and alumina producer with mines, refineries and smelters worldwide.
AA.bull: Q3 EPS beat by 22% with $472M of free cash flow; trades at ~7x earnings and ~3.5x EBITDA.
AA.bear: Revenue missed slightly; Q4 has ~$60M of headwinds and a ~$3.1B acquisition to fund.
AA.take: Cheap and cash-generative; the aluminum price decides the rest.

AAPL.name: Apple
AAPL.about: Maker of iPhone, Mac and wearables plus a large services business.
AAPL.bull: Foldable iPhone Duo preorders sold out; services keep margins high (27.6% net).
AAPL.bear: Trades above the average analyst target ($329) at ~37x forward earnings; earlier reports of iPhone 18 Pro order cuts.
AAPL.take: A quality name priced for a strong product cycle.

AGIO.name: Agios Pharmaceuticals
AGIO.about: Rare-blood-disease drugmaker selling mitapivat (Pyrukynd, Aqvesme) for PK deficiency and thalassemia.
AGIO.bull: An FDA decision Nov 1 could add sickle cell, its largest market; net cash ~$934M is about half the market cap.
AGIO.bear: The Phase 3 missed on pain crises, so the FDA could reject or narrow the label; ~$365M yearly burn; 15% short.
AGIO.take: A steadier biotech binary: the cash limits the downside, while the label sets the upside.
AGIO.catalyst: FDA decision on mitapivat for sickle cell disease (priority review, accelerated approval)
AGIO.runway: StockAnalysis puts net cash near $934M including longer-term investments, about 2.5 years at the current burn.

AMAT.name: Applied Materials
AMAT.bull: 30% net margins; AI chip capacity needs more tools.
AMAT.bear: China export limits and cyclical spending.
AMAT.take: Quality name hit by a sector-wide selloff.

AMD.name: Advanced Micro Devices
AMD.about: Designs CPUs and AI accelerator GPUs (Instinct) for data centers and PCs.
AMD.bull: AI GPU share gains and server CPU strength; revenue $41.3B TTM with 15.6% net margin.
AMD.bear: Trades at ~48x forward earnings and fell 6% on Oct 16 as AI capex doubts spread.
AMD.take: A high-beta (2.45) way to own AI chips; sentiment on AI spending drives it more than fundamentals week to week.

ANAB.name: AnaptysBio
ANAB.about: Antibody biotech living on royalties (including GSK's Jemperli) that originated imsidolimab, now licensed to Vanda.
ANAB.bull: Royalty income makes it profitable; an imsidolimab approval Dec 12 adds another income stream. Target ~76% above.
ANAB.bear: Profits depend heavily on a few royalties; short interest is high at ~27%.
ANAB.take: A royalty company with a free option on Vanda's Dec 12 decision.

ANNX.name: Annexon
ANNX.about: Complement-blocking antibodies for eye and nerve diseases; also filing a Guillain-Barré syndrome drug.
ANNX.bull: Two shots on goal: GA Phase 3 in Q4 plus a GBS approval path (EU review, US filing). Target ~3.7x price.
ANNX.bear: Geographic atrophy has a history of failed trials; ~$190M yearly burn means dilution if data disappoints.
ANNX.take: The largest potential payoff in the Moonshots, but also the hardest trial to win.
ANNX.catalyst: Phase 3 ARCHER II topline for vonaprument in geographic atrophy (a cause of blindness)

APA.name: APA Corporation
APA.about: Independent oil and gas producer exploring for and producing crude oil, natural gas and NGLs in the US, Egypt and the North Sea.
APA.bull: Brent near $104-105 on Iran and Hormuz tensions flows quickly into earnings for a producer this sensitive to crude.
APA.bear: The stock is up about 74% in a year and near its 52-week high, so a de-escalation could take the oil premium back out fast.
APA.take: Cheap at about 3x EV/EBITDA, but that cheapness is tied to oil prices that are being driven by headlines.

APLD.name: Applied Digital
APLD.about: Builds and runs high-power data-center campuses for AI and cloud tenants.
APLD.bull: Large leased AI capacity; average target $64 is ~2.9x the price.
APLD.bear: Net margin -53%, beta 6, and 22% of the float short; dependent on capital markets.
APLD.take: High-beta AI infrastructure name that moves with funding sentiment.

ASTS.name: AST SpaceMobile
ASTS.about: Satellites that connect directly to ordinary phones.
ASTS.bull: Carrier partnerships (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone); revenue nearly tripled.
ASTS.bear: ~200x sales; competes with Starlink direct-to-cell; 17% short interest.

AU.name: AngloGold Ashanti
AU.about: Global gold miner with mines in Africa, Australia and the Americas.
AU.bull: Goldman initiated at Buy ($104); ~10x forward earnings, ~3.9% yield.
AU.bear: Gold has fallen from highs on hike bets; country risk in Africa.
AU.take: A cheaper large gold miner if bullion holds $4,100+.

AVAV.name: AeroVironment
AVAV.about: Small drones, Switchblade loitering munitions, and space/cyber via BlueHalo.
AVAV.bull: ~57% upside to target; drone warfare demand.
AVAV.bear: Acquisition costs pushed it to a net loss.
AVAV.take: Big gap to target after integrating BlueHalo.

AVGO.name: Broadcom
AVGO.about: Broadcom designs and supplies semiconductor devices and infrastructure software worldwide.
AVGO.bull: Broadcom's custom AI chips (including Google's TPUs) and networking are growing ~49% a year, and it may guarantee debt for Anthropic's TPU buildout.
AVGO.bear: Customer concentration in a few hyperscalers and exposure to AI-financing stress; still ~31x EBITDA.
AVGO.take: A core AI-supply-chain name; the Anthropic financing shows both its pull and the credit risk building around it.

AXP.name: American Express
AXP.about: American Express is a global payments company that issues credit and charge cards and offers related travel and expense services.
AXP.bull: Affluent card members keep spending; strong credit and buybacks.
AXP.bear: Fintech rivals like Ramp target corporate cards; consumer slowdown risk.
AXP.take: A high-quality lender; the threat from startups is slow, not sudden.

AZN.name: AstraZeneca
AZN.about: Global biopharma company that discovers, develops and sells prescription medicines in oncology, rare disease, cardiovascular and respiratory care.
AZN.bull: Enhertu remains a standout HER2 drug and the broad pipeline supports analyst targets near $207.
AZN.bear: FDA approval of Pfizer's Tukysa as first-line maintenance adds competition in HER2+ metastatic breast cancer, where Enhertu competes.
AZN.take: Trading near its 52-week low at about 15x forward earnings; one new HER2 rival matters less than the depth of the overall portfolio.

BAC.name: Bank of America
BAC.bull: About 10x forward earnings and 1.3x book; the $1.2B penalty is one-off.
BAC.bear: Q3 revenue missed; regulators' AML findings may bring more costs.
BAC.take: Cheap, but needs clean quarters to re-rate.

BILL.name: BILL Holdings
BILL.about: BILL provides a financial operations platform covering payables, receivables, payments and spend management for small and midsize businesses.
BILL.bull: Growing ~13% with a cheap ~2.4x sales multiple; a takeover target for buyers of software.
BILL.bear: Ramp and others are taking share; small businesses are sensitive to the economy.
BILL.take: A cheap listed comparison for richly valued private fintech.

BK.name: BNY
BK.about: World's largest custody bank (formerly BNY Mellon).
BK.bull: Q3 net income +20%; fees rise with asset prices.
BK.bear: Fee revenue falls if markets drop.
BK.take: A fee machine benefiting from high asset prices.

BLK.name: BlackRock, Inc.
BLK.about: World's largest asset manager, serving institutional and retail investors with funds, ETFs (iShares), risk tools and advisory services.
BLK.take: Listed comparable for a private-markets idea; use its multiples to sanity-check private valuations.

BMNR.name: BitMine Immersion
BMNR.bull: Leveraged to ETH and the Glamsterdam upgrade; trades near book.
BMNR.bear: ETH down 39% YoY; value is mostly the token holdings.
BMNR.take: ETH proxy. Compare price to net asset value before buying.

BMY.name: Bristol Myers Squibb
BMY.about: Large pharma (Eliquis, Opdivo) facing a patent cliff, rebuilding with new drugs.
BMY.bull: Two Phase 3 wins (admilparant in IPF, RYZ101 in neuroendocrine tumors); ~9.3x forward earnings and a 4.5% dividend.
BMY.bear: Only the lower admilparant dose worked; patent expiries still weigh on revenue.
BMY.take: Cheap pharma with fresh pipeline proof; label details for admilparant are the next test.

BORR.name: Borr Drilling
BORR.about: Bermuda-based owner of a modern fleet of shallow-water jackup drilling rigs.
BORR.bull: Director Tor Olav Trøim has bought ~10M shares (now 12.2%); ~9.8x EV/EBITDA with oil above $100.
BORR.bear: $2.49B debt vs $224M cash, negative free cash flow and ~20% more shares in a year.
BORR.take: A leveraged bet on offshore drilling demand, backed by heavy insider buying.

BX.name: Blackstone
BX.about: Largest alternative asset manager (PE, real estate, credit).
BX.bull: Fee-earning AUM keeps growing and deal activity is picking up; 4.5% dividend.
BX.bear: Private-credit redemptions and real-estate marks can hit fees and sentiment.
BX.take: The main listed proxy for the private-markets cycle; reportedly bidding for Finastra.

BYRN.name: Byrna Technologies
BYRN.about: Makes Byrna CO2-powered non-lethal launchers and ammunition for personal and police use.
BYRN.bull: Six insiders bought ~$400K of stock in the open market at ~$3.77 (Form 4s filed Oct 16) after an ~80% slide; the company is still FCF-positive with almost no debt, and B. Riley keeps a Buy ($11 target).
BYRN.bear: Q3 sales fell 46% to $15.3M with a $2.9M loss; cash is only ~$9.4M and two big international customers went bad.
BYRN.take: A cheap turnaround with insider support; holiday-quarter sales are the proof point.
BYRN.catalyst: Fiscal Q4 (holiday quarter) results and new retail door expansion in Q1 2027
BYRN.runway: About $9.4M cash, no debt and slightly positive free cash flow; little cushion if sales keep falling, though planned inventory cuts ($2–3M in Q4) should free cash.

CAPR.name: Capricor Therapeutics
CAPR.about: Cell-therapy company whose deramiocel treats heart and muscle decline in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
CAPR.bull: Phase 3 HOPE-3 hit its primary endpoint; FDA decision Nov 22; ~$238M cash and a $27 average target vs $7.75.
CAPR.bear: Fell ~13% on Oct 5 after open-label extension data that had no statistical testing; ~46% of the float is sold short. A rejection on Nov 22 would be a big drop.
CAPR.take: Pure binary into Nov 22. Analysts are split (Roth constructive, H.C. Wainwright expects a rejection letter), so size for a wide range of outcomes.
CAPR.catalyst: FDA decision on deramiocel (Duchenne, upper-limb function)
CAPR.runway: ~$238M cash vs ~$130M yearly burn: roughly 18 months without a raise.

CCCS.name: CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc.
CCCS.about: Cloud SaaS platform connecting auto insurers, repairers, automakers and partners in the P&C insurance claims ecosystem.
CCCS.bull: Signed $7.75 cash deal with GTCR and Elliott (~$6.1B EV) with committed JPM/Citi financing.
CCCS.bear: Upside is capped at $7.75 (~1.6% spread); a regulatory or vote problem would send it back toward $5.

CCI.name: Crown Castle
CCI.about: Owns ~40,000 US cell towers leased to carriers.
CCI.bull: A fourth carrier would need tower space; +11.3% on the SpaceX news; ~5.3% yield.
CCI.bear: Its main tenants (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile) are now under pressure.
CCI.take: A landlord that wins if competition increases, as long as the incumbents keep paying rent.

CENX.name: Century Aluminum
CENX.about: US and Iceland aluminum smelter operator.
CENX.bull: Very cheap at ~2.6x forward earnings; US tariffs on imported aluminum support domestic prices.
CENX.bear: Power costs and high beta (2.1); 13% of the float is sold short.
CENX.take: A small, leveraged play on US aluminum prices.

CGON.name: CG Oncology
CGON.about: Developing cretostimogene, a virus-based bladder-cancer therapy.
CGON.bear: Pre-revenue; Anktiva's broader label raises the bar.
CGON.take: A mid-cap bladder-cancer rival to watch into its filing.

CMG.name: Chipotle Mexican Grill
CMG.about: Fast-casual Mexican restaurant chain (burritos, bowls, tacos) with ~$12B in yearly sales.
CMG.bull: FT says Starbucks explored a takeover that could cost ~$50B; the stock is still well below its 52-week high.
CMG.bear: No offer has been made and the deal may never happen; same-store traffic has been soft.
CMG.take: Takeover talk puts a floor under it, but don't count on a bid.

CMPS.name: COMPASS Pathways
CMPS.about: Developing COMP360 psilocybin therapy for treatment-resistant depression.
CMPS.bull: ~$433M cash and a Strong Buy consensus with target ~2x price.
CMPS.bear: Burning ~$161M a year; regulators have been cautious on psychedelics.
CMPS.take: Sector leader whose data and FDA path set the tone for Helus.

COGT.name: Cogent Biosciences
COGT.about: Clinical-stage cancer biotech whose lead drug bezuclastinib targets KIT-driven GIST and systemic mastocytosis.
COGT.bull: First FDA decision (GIST, priority review) is due Nov 30; analysts' target is ~85% above the price and cash is ~$792M.
COGT.bear: Burns ~$309M a year and share count rose ~38% in a year; a rejection or weak launch would hurt.
COGT.take: A mid-cap binary with a cash cushion; the Nov 30 decision is the swing factor.

COIN.name: Coinbase
COIN.about: Largest US crypto exchange and custodian; runs the Base network.
COIN.bull: Trading volume recovers when bitcoin trends up; custody for most bitcoin ETFs.
COIN.bear: Net loss over the last year; very high beta (3.4).
COIN.take: Leveraged to crypto activity, not just price.

CORT.name: Corcept Therapeutics
CORT.about: Sells Korlym for Cushing's syndrome and develops cortisol-modulating drugs like relacorilant.
CORT.bull: Profitable ($831M TTM revenue) with net cash ~$535M and a Dec 17 FDA decision on relacorilant.
CORT.bear: Up ~280% from its 52-week low, so approval is largely priced in; a second rejection would hurt.
CORT.take: A profitable biotech with a binary event; expectations are already high.

CRML.name: Critical Metals
CRML.about: Mining exploration and development company working on the Tanbreez rare-earth project in Greenland and lithium in Europe.
CRML.bull: If China reimposes rare-earth export controls when the truce expires Nov 10, non-Chinese supply projects like Tanbreez could draw more interest.
CRML.bear: It has almost no revenue, is far below its 52-week high, and over 30% of the float is sold short.
CRML.take: A speculative bet on rare-earth politics; the Nov 10 deadline can move the stock sharply in either direction.

CRWV.name: CoreWeave
CRWV.about: GPU cloud provider renting Nvidia chips to AI labs, funded largely with debt.
CRWV.bull: Revenue ~$7.6B TTM and a ~$141 average target, more than double the price.
CRWV.bear: Net margin -25%, bond yields near 15% and 18% of the float short.
CRWV.take: A leveraged bet on AI demand; credit markets now set the stock's direction.

CXM.name: Sprinklr
CXM.about: Enterprise customer-experience software (social, contact center, marketing) for large brands.
CXM.bull: $453M cash vs $41M debt, $128M FCF (~9% yield), shares down ~8% YoY from buybacks; director bought $850K on Oct 13.
CXM.bear: Revenue flat (+0.8% last quarter); consensus is only Hold; AI could compress seat-based contact-center software.
CXM.take: A steadier Moonshot: cheap on cash flow with insider buying; the upside needs growth or a buyer.
CXM.catalyst: Next quarterly results (date TBA); continued buybacks and insider buying
CXM.runway: No runway issue: net cash of ~$410M and positive free cash flow.

CYTK.name: Cytokinetics
CYTK.about: Heart-muscle drug developer; aficamten treats obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
CYTK.bull: ~$1.2B of cash and a Nov 14 FDA decision on MAPLE-HCM data that could widen use vs Camzyos.
CYTK.bear: Still early in sales ($68M TTM revenue) with heavy losses; down ~30% from its 52-week high.
CYTK.take: A mid-cap heart-drug launch story; the Nov 14 label is the near-term swing factor.

DAL.name: Delta Air Lines
DAL.about: Largest US airline by revenue; premium-heavy customer mix.
DAL.bull: Jet fuel is a huge cost; cheaper oil flows straight to profit. ~23% upside to target.
DAL.bear: Q3 missed slightly and the 2026 EPS guide was cut to $5.10–5.60 from $6.50–7.50 on a ~$6B higher fuel bill.
DAL.take: Demand is fine; the stock is a bet on oil falling.

DGX.name: Quest Diagnostics
DGX.about: Largest US independent clinical lab operator.
DGX.bear: Faces a larger Labcorp after the BioReference deal.
DGX.take: The steady half of the lab duopoly.

DHI.name: D.R. Horton
DHI.bull: Fewer Fed hikes would ease mortgage rates; 1.6x book.
DHI.bear: 10-year at 5.3% keeps mortgage rates high and buyers away.
DHI.take: Pure rates trade. Watch the 10-year more than the company.

DHT.name: DHT Holdings
DHT.about: Owner of a fleet of very large crude carriers (VLCCs) that pays out most of its earnings as dividends.
DHT.bull: Its VLCC Antelope was fixed at a record ~$1.16M a day for a Gulf of Oman load; ~7.5% yield.
DHT.bear: Already above the analyst target; rates can collapse if Hormuz traffic normalizes.
DHT.take: The purest public play on record tanker rates, but it is a crisis trade.

DRS.name: Leonardo DRS
DRS.about: US defense electronics maker (sensors, radars, power and propulsion), majority-owned by Italy's Leonardo.
DRS.bull: New $500M counter-drone IDIQ; ~52% upside to its average target; Strong Buy consensus.
DRS.bear: ~26x forward earnings; IDIQ ceilings are not guaranteed revenue.
DRS.take: A mid-cap way to play counter-drone spending.

DXYZ.name: Destiny Tech100 Inc.
DXYZ.about: Closed-end fund holding stakes in late-stage private venture-backed tech companies.
DXYZ.bull: Gives retail access to late-stage private tech like SpaceX-era holdings.
DXYZ.bear: Often trades far above or below the value of its holdings.
DXYZ.take: A sentiment gauge for private tech, not a cheap entry.

ENTG.name: Entegris
ENTG.about: Supplier of advanced materials, filters and process products used in semiconductor manufacturing.
ENTG.bull: Samsung's record Q3 profit on AI memory points to busy memory fabs, which use more of Entegris's materials.
ENTG.bear: At 37x forward earnings and up a lot from its 52-week low, the stock already prices in a strong recovery, and it trades near the analyst target.
ENTG.take: It slipped on Oct 7 despite Samsung's strong guide, which suggests investors already expect the memory upturn; delivery now matters more than the headline.

ERO.name: Ero Copper
ERO.about: Small-mid cap copper miner operating in Brazil.
ERO.bull: 8x forward; copper plus a Brazil tailwind.
ERO.take: Cheapest copper producer here on forward earnings.

FCX.name: Freeport-McMoRan
FCX.bull: Copper demand from AI data centers and the grid.
FCX.take: Benchmark copper name; little upside priced by analysts.

FRO.name: Frontline
FRO.about: One of the largest crude-tanker owners (VLCCs, Suezmax).
FRO.bull: Hormuz disruption keeps tanker day rates very high; pays big variable dividends.
FRO.bear: Trades above the analyst target; a real Hormuz reopening would crush rates.
FRO.take: Earning a windfall; the stock is a bet on how long the disruption lasts.

FUN.name: Six Flags Entertainment
FUN.about: Largest regional theme-park operator in North America (Six Flags, Cedar Point).
FUN.bull: Trades at ~0.35x sales and ~7.9x EV/EBITDA; analysts' $20 target is ~2x the price.
FUN.bear: A fatal ride accident, weak attendance, heavy debt, a -57% net margin and 25% short interest.
FUN.take: Deep value or value trap; the balance sheet decides.

GCMG.name: GCM Grosvenor
GCMG.about: Alternatives manager focused on co-investments, secondaries and customized private-markets portfolios.
GCMG.bull: Co-investing in Viridor with AIMCo; 3.7% yield and ~13x forward earnings.
GCMG.bear: Small scale versus giants; fee pressure.
GCMG.take: A small-cap way to own private-markets fee growth.

GD.name: General Dynamics
GD.about: Defense prime (Electric Boat submarines, combat vehicles) plus Gulfstream business jets.
GD.bull: Electric Boat has a huge submarine backlog; more supplier capacity (even from Anduril) eases its bottleneck.
GD.bear: Sub programs run late and over budget; Gulfstream ties it to the business cycle.
GD.take: Steady large-cap; the Anduril news is more competition at the edges than a threat to its core.

GLXY.name: Galaxy Digital
GLXY.about: Crypto trading, asset management and a data-center business.
GLXY.bull: Target ~76% above price; AI data-center (Helios) adds a second leg.
GLXY.bear: Breakeven at best; trading revenue swings with crypto.
GLXY.take: Mid-cap crypto financial with an AI option.

GM.name: General Motors
GM.about: Automaker that designs, builds and sells trucks, crossovers and cars, plus related parts and financing.
GM.bull: Under 6x forward earnings and well below the analyst target, with strong truck and SUV profits.
GM.bear: EV motors need rare-earth magnets, so if China reimposes export controls after the Nov 10 truce ends, GM's supply could be disrupted.
GM.take: Cheap on earnings, but the rare-earth deadline is a real supply-chain risk to watch.

GOOGL.name: Alphabet
GOOGL.about: Alphabet runs Google Services, Google Cloud and Other Bets, including search, YouTube, Android and cloud computing.
GOOGL.bull: Search, YouTube and Cloud are growing ~20% with very high margins, and TPUs give it a second AI business.
GOOGL.bear: AI chatbots could erode search; heavy capex and antitrust remedies.
GOOGL.take: Profitable AI leader at ~17x trailing earnings; TPU demand from Anthropic is a growing bonus.

GS.name: Goldman Sachs
GS.about: Investment bank and asset manager with a large alternatives arm.
GS.bull: Q3 EPS $17.01 vs ~$13.02 expected; equities trading +72% and banking fees +21%.
GS.bear: Trading results swing with markets; private-credit exposure is in focus.
GS.take: Best bank print of the season; a read that deal activity is truly recovering.

GSK.name: GSK plc
GSK.bull: Under 10x forward earnings with a 3.8% yield; bepirovirsen could be a first-in-class hepatitis B drug.
GSK.bear: Low growth (~4%) and HIV patent risks later this decade.
GSK.take: Value-priced pharma with a near-term FDA catalyst.

GTM.name: ZoomInfo Technologies
GTM.about: B2B contact and company data provider for sales teams.
GTM.bear: Revenue shrinking; losing share to AI-native tools like Clay.
GTM.take: Shows how the market prices a disrupted data incumbent.

HBM.name: Hudbay Minerals
HBM.about: Copper and gold mines in Peru, Canada and the US (Arizona project).
HBM.take: Mid-cap copper with a long pipeline.

HELP.name: Helus Pharma (formerly Cybin)
HELP.about: Develops psychedelic-derived drugs; lead HLP003 (CYB003) in Phase 3 for depression.
HELP.bull: Phase 3 APPROACH fully enrolled with data due Q4 2026; four insiders bought ~$6.3M on Oct 1; target ~3.5x price.
HELP.bear: Share count doubled in a year; burns ~$140M a year; a Phase 3 miss would hit the stock hard.
HELP.take: Binary but well-funded: insiders buying right before data is a meaningful signal.
HELP.catalyst: Phase 3 APPROACH topline for HLP003 in major depressive disorder
