HELP.runway: ~$166M cash (June 30) vs ~$141M yearly burn: about a year, so a raise after data is likely.

HL.name: Hecla Mining
HL.about: Largest US silver producer, also mining gold, lead and zinc in the US and Canada.
HL.bull: Silver near $60 still supports strong margins, and analysts see the stock well above the current price.
HL.bear: Gold at a two-month low on rate-hike bets and 5%+ yields could drag silver further, and Hecla's high beta amplifies the move.
HL.take: Down about half from its 52-week high; this stock tends to move more than silver itself in both directions.

HOOD.name: Robinhood
HOOD.about: Retail brokerage with large crypto and options volume.
HOOD.bull: Profitable (42% net margin); benefits from any retail risk-on.
HOOD.take: Quality way to play retail and crypto activity.

HWBK.name: Hawthorn Bancshares
HWBK.bull: 10x earnings, 2.2% dividend, net income rising (Q2 $7.3M vs $6.1M), insiders buying, near its 52-week low.
HWBK.bear: Slow growth; only ~1.4x book; no analyst coverage; exposed to local credit and deposit costs.
HWBK.take: The 'quiet diamond': little analyst coverage, insiders buying, low volatility. Upside is slower but sturdier.
HWBK.catalyst: Executives and directors bought shares in 2026; Q3 earnings in late October
HWBK.runway: Profitable community bank; buying back shares.

IBRX.name: ImmunityBio
IBRX.about: Maker of Anktiva, an immunotherapy for bladder cancer.
IBRX.bull: Label just expanded; sales grew fast from a small base.
IBRX.bear: ~65x sales, losses, and 30% of the float short.
IBRX.take: The approval helps, but the valuation already assumes big growth.

IMMR.name: Immersion
IMMR.about: Haptics patent licensor that controls and consolidates Barnes & Noble Education (college bookstores).
IMMR.bull: About 4.8x EV/EBITDA, ~$61M free cash flow (~26% of market value), a 4.2% dividend, and the CEO bought ~41,000 shares at ~$7.13 on Oct 7.
IMMR.bear: Net margin only 0.6%; bookstore retail is low-growth; filings have run late (Nasdaq delinquency notice, March 2026); no analyst coverage; debt of ~$273M exceeds cash of ~$210M.
IMMR.take: A steadier Moonshot: the upside is a re-rating of cheap cash flow, not a binary event.
IMMR.catalyst: Next quarterly report (fiscal Q2 2027) and continued insider buying; ex-dividend Oct 16
IMMR.runway: Generates positive free cash flow (~$61M TTM) and pays a dividend, so it needs no outside capital.

INO.name: INOVIO Pharmaceuticals
INO.about: DNA-medicine company whose lead drug, INO-3107, treats a rare HPV disease that grows tumors in the airway.
INO.bull: Late-cycle FDA meeting and inspections are done; Breakthrough and Orphan status; an approval would be its first product, at a ~$120M valuation.
INO.bear: Share count nearly doubled in a year; even with approval it will likely need to raise money again in early 2027. Now trading just under $1 (Oct 16 close $0.99), which risks a Nasdaq minimum-bid notice if it stays there.
INO.take: Classic binary setup: one FDA decision on Oct 30 decides most of the value. Size it so a zero is survivable.
INO.catalyst: FDA decision on INO-3107 (accelerated approval) for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
INO.runway: About $37M cash (incl. a July raise) and ~$18M/quarter burn; company guides runway into late Q1 2027.

INSM.name: Insmed
INSM.about: Biopharma company selling Arikayce, an inhaled treatment for a rare lung infection, and Brinsupri (brensocatib) for bronchiectasis.
INSM.bull: Arikayce shows how valuable an inhaled rare-lung drug can be, and analysts' targets are nearly double the current price.
INSM.bear: The company is still losing money and the stock is down more than half from its 52-week high.
INSM.take: Savara's Nov 22 FDA date highlights the market for rare-lung drugs; Insmed is already selling one but has not yet turned a profit.

INTC.name: Intel
INTC.about: PC and server chipmaker rebuilding its foundry business.
INTC.bull: Stock has more than doubled in a year on the foundry turnaround; analysts' target ~$118.
INTC.bear: Still loss-making (-19.8% net margin) and fell 5.8% Oct 16 in the chip selloff.
INTC.take: Oct 29 Q3 results (guide up to $16.8B) are the next test of the turnaround.

IONS.name: Ionis Pharmaceuticals
IONS.about: RNA-targeting drug developer with several launched and partnered medicines.
IONS.bull: Revenue up 26%; hepatitis B drug bepirovirsen (with GSK) has an FDA date Oct 26; targets ~1.9x price.
IONS.bear: Still loss-making (-65% net margin); 12.6% of float sold short.
IONS.take: Several shots on goal this quarter; the Oct 26 decision is the nearest.

IRD.name: Opus Genetics
IRD.about: Eye-care company: phentolamine drops (already approved for another use) plus gene therapies for inherited blindness.
IRD.bull: Presbyopia affects over a billion people; the drop worked for up to 20 hours in Phase 3 and avoids the side effects of rival drops. Analysts' target is ~2.8x the price.
IRD.bear: Share count more than doubled in a year. Earlier presbyopia drops (like Vuity) sold slower than hoped.
IRD.take: FDA approved RYZUMVI for presbyopia on Oct 16; the stock fell 5% on the news. Now a launch story run by Viatris.
IRD.catalyst: Viatris US launch of RYZUMVI for presbyopia; approval milestone payment
IRD.runway: About $89M cash vs ~$41M yearly burn: roughly two years, but an approval-led launch would likely need more money.

ITUB.name: Itaú Unibanco
ITUB.bear: Already above analyst target after +15% in a day.
ITUB.take: Rally may have run ahead of fundamentals.

JBLU.name: JetBlue Airways
JBLU.about: Small-cap airline; unprofitable and heavily indebted.
JBLU.bull: Most leveraged to a fuel-price drop; 25% short interest could squeeze.
JBLU.bear: Analyst consensus is Sell; balance sheet risk if recession hits.

KKR.name: KKR & Co.
KKR.about: Global alternatives manager in private equity, credit, infrastructure and insurance (Global Atlantic).
KKR.bull: Just closed a $300B fundraise; ~12x forward earnings with a target ~35% above the price.
KKR.bear: Slow PE exits delay carried interest; high beta (1.8) to markets and rates.
KKR.take: A scaled winner as LP money concentrates in fewer managers.

KO.name: Coca-Cola
KO.about: Coca-Cola makes and sells nonalcoholic beverages worldwide.
KO.bull: Pricing power and share wins such as the reported KFC switch; steady dividend.
KO.bear: Expensive at ~28x earnings near a 52-week high; GLP-1 and sugar-tax risks.
KO.take: A defensive compounder; good news looks largely priced in.

KTOS.name: Kratos Defense
KTOS.about: Low-cost combat drones, hypersonic test vehicles and satellite ground systems.
KTOS.bull: Analyst target is ~2.4x the price; cheaper, faster procurement fits its products.
KTOS.bear: Thin profits; the stock has already collapsed from much higher levels, so momentum is weak.
KTOS.take: Biggest gap to target in the defense tower. Find out why it fell before buying.

LEN.name: Lennar
LEN.bull: Berkshire owns ~12%; trades below book value with a ~2.6% dividend.
LEN.bear: Margins are being squeezed by incentives with mortgage rates near 7%+; consensus rating is Sell.
LEN.take: A value bet on housing that needs rates to fall to really work.

LH.name: Labcorp Holdings
LH.about: One of the two largest US clinical lab and drug-development testing companies.
LH.bull: Buying BioReference assets for up to $872M adds volume; steady ~17x forward earnings.
LH.bear: Low growth (~5% forecast) and reimbursement pressure.
LH.take: A defensive consolidator; the deal fits its tuck-in playbook.

LHX.name: L3Harris Technologies
LHX.about: Defense electronics and, via Aerojet Rocketdyne, missile rocket motors.
LHX.bull: Rocket-motor demand rises with every interceptor deal.
LHX.bear: Motor production has a history of delays.
LHX.take: A picks-and-shovels play on the missile build-up.

LULU.name: Lululemon Athletica
LULU.bull: About 8x earnings and ~5x EV/EBITDA with a 13% net margin.
LULU.bear: Revenue forecast to shrink; 15% short interest shows heavy skepticism.
LULU.take: Priced for decline; a cheap stock that needs a growth story.

META.name: Meta Platforms
META.about: Meta builds social apps such as Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, plus VR headsets and AI glasses.
META.bull: Ads are growing ~28% and AI is improving targeting; strong cash flow funds its buildout.
META.bear: Very large AI capex with uncertain payback; regulatory and youth-safety risks.
META.take: Its Oct 21 capex guide is the week's key AI-spending signal.

MLYS.name: Mineralys Therapeutics
MLYS.about: Single-product biotech developing lorundrostat, an aldosterone-synthase blocker for hard-to-treat high blood pressure.
MLYS.bull: FDA decision Dec 22 after a 1,083-patient Phase 3; ~$661M cash and royalty-free economics; target ~2x the price.
MLYS.bear: One drug; AstraZeneca's baxdrostat competes; share count up 46% in a year and launch costs will raise burn.
MLYS.take: A well-funded approval bet rather than a lottery ticket, but still binary on one FDA decision.
MLYS.catalyst: FDA decision on lorundrostat for uncontrolled hypertension (with other BP drugs)
MLYS.runway: Company guides cash into 2028, including the launch.

MP.name: MP Materials
MP.about: Only scaled US rare-earth miner and magnet maker; the Pentagon is a major shareholder.
MP.bull: Government price floor and offtake; ~57% upside to target.

MRCY.name: Mercury Systems
MRCY.about: Makes defense electronics such as processing modules and subsystems sold to prime contractors and governments.
MRCY.bull: If Boeing triples PAC-3 seeker output, suppliers of missile electronics like Mercury could see more orders (an inferred link).
MRCY.bear: It is still unprofitable on a net basis, trades near 48x forward earnings, and about 9% of the float is sold short.
MRCY.take: A possible second-order beneficiary of higher missile production, but the link is inferred and the valuation already assumes a recovery.

MRK.name: Merck & Co.
MRK.about: Big pharma behind Keytruda and partner on Moderna's cancer vaccine.
MRK.bull: A vaccine win would extend Keytruda's franchise; ~17x forward earnings.
MRK.take: Lower-risk way to own the cancer-vaccine readout.

MRNA.name: Moderna
MRNA.about: mRNA medicines: COVID and RSV vaccines plus a personalized cancer vaccine with Merck.
MRNA.bull: Phase 3 melanoma-vaccine data at ESMO could open a large oncology market.
MRNA.bear: Trades far above the average target (~$123) after a huge run; still losing money.
MRNA.take: Priced for a clean win; the Oct 24 webcast is the test.

MS.name: Morgan Stanley
MS.bull: Beat Q3 on deals and equities; wealth unit gives steady fees.
MS.bear: Trading and deal fees are cyclical; higher rates could cool IPOs.
MS.take: One of the cleaner Q3 bank prints.

MSTR.name: Strategy (MicroStrategy)
MSTR.about: Holds a huge bitcoin treasury funded by stock and debt.
MSTR.bear: Bitcoin is down 29% YoY; leverage works both ways.
MSTR.take: A leveraged bitcoin position, not an operating business.

MTH.name: Meritage Homes
MTH.about: Builds entry-level and first move-up single-family homes across 12 US states and offers mortgage and title services.
MTH.bull: It trades below book value, so a drop in mortgage rates could lift the shares quickly.
MTH.bear: With 30-year mortgages near 7.5%, its first-time buyers are the most squeezed, and Truist flagged it as the most exposed builder.
MTH.take: Cheap on book value but sitting near its 52-week low with revenue shrinking 13%; direction depends mostly on rates.

MU.name: Micron
MU.about: The largest US memory maker: DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and SSDs.
MU.bull: Revenue up nearly 4x YoY and 7x forward earnings.
MU.bear: Memory is the most cyclical part of chips. A low P/E at peak earnings is a classic trap.
MU.take: Cheap if the upcycle lasts. Watch DRAM contract prices for the first sign of a turn.

NBIS.name: Nebius Group
NBIS.about: Amsterdam-based AI cloud and GPU infrastructure company.
NBIS.bull: Fast growth and less debt than CoreWeave; average target ~$284.
NBIS.take: Priced for flawless execution; moves with neocloud sentiment.

NEM.name: Newmont
NEM.about: The world's largest gold miner, with copper, silver and zinc output from mines on several continents.
NEM.bull: Even after the dip, gold near $4,100 keeps margins above 30% and the stock trades at under 7x EV/EBITDA.
NEM.bear: Its profits move with the gold price, so further rate-hike bets and 5%+ yields that pushed gold to a 2-month low hit earnings directly.
NEM.take: A leveraged gold proxy; the near-term swing factor is whether rising yields keep pressuring the metal.

NKE.name: Nike
NKE.about: World's largest athletic footwear and apparel brand.
NKE.bull: 4.4% dividend yield and a deeply cut share price; any demand recovery would re-rate it.
NKE.bear: Shares down ~42% this year; forward P/E (27x) is above trailing as earnings fall.
NKE.take: A turnaround bet; Oct 15 bounce came with falling yields, not new news.

NOC.name: Northrop Grumman
NOC.about: Defense prime: B-21 bomber, Sentinel ICBM, space and missile parts.
NOC.bull: Missile and munitions ramp; ~25% below the average target.
NOC.bear: Fixed-price programs can run over budget.
NOC.take: Steady defense compounder with munitions upside.

NU.name: Nu Holdings
NU.about: Digital bank (Nubank) with 100M+ customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
NU.bull: Jumped 13% on the vote; still ~23% below the average target.
NU.bear: A Lula comeback on Oct 25 would likely reverse the rally.
NU.take: Highest-quality Brazil name; the runoff is the near-term swing factor.

NVDA.name: NVIDIA
NVDA.about: Designs the GPUs and networking that most AI training and inference runs on.
NVDA.bull: Blackwell and Rubin demand still exceeds supply; Google, Microsoft and others keep raising capex.
NVDA.bear: Customers like Google are building their own chips (TPUs), which caps Nvidia's share long term.
NVDA.take: 25x forward earnings for 100%+ revenue growth is not expensive by its own history; the risk is the cycle, not the multiple.

ON.name: onsemi
ON.about: onsemi makes power and sensing semiconductors for automotive, industrial and other applications.
ON.bull: Power chips for EVs, industrial and AI data centers; trades well below its 52-week high with a recovery expected.
ON.bear: EV demand is soft and revenue is still falling slightly; SiC competition is intense.
ON.take: A cyclical recovery play tied to EVs and data-center power.

ONDS.name: Ondas Holdings
ONDS.about: Drone, counter-drone and defense-component maker built through acquisitions.
ONDS.bull: Revenue nearly tripled; new $56M munitions order; analysts' target ~2.6x price.
ONDS.bear: ~42% of float sold short; growth is acquisition-driven and needs to show organic delivery.
ONDS.take: Fast-growing but crowded short; expect big swings.

OPK.name: OPKO Health
OPK.about: Miami diagnostics and pharma company (BioReference labs, Rayaldee, partnered drugs).
OPK.bull: Up to $872M from Labcorp is a large share of its ~$1.1B value; ~3x average target.
OPK.bear: Losing money (-12% margin); a penny-stock price and a history of dilution.
OPK.take: The asset sale turns a cash drain into cash; the question is what is left.

PAAS.name: Pan American Silver
PAAS.about: Large silver and gold miner across the Americas.
PAAS.bull: ~10x forward earnings with 32% net margins; targets ~43% above price.
PAAS.bear: Gold/silver prices pinned by 5%+ yields and a strong dollar.
PAAS.take: The lower-risk way to own silver upside.

PBR.name: Petrobras
PBR.bull: 4.5x forward earnings, ~5% dividend; a Bolsonaro win is seen as market-friendly.
PBR.bear: Now above the average target; political control of pricing and dividends.
PBR.take: Cheap, but the price now assumes the Oct 25 runoff goes the market's way.

PEP.name: PepsiCo
PEP.about: PepsiCo makes, markets and sells beverages and convenience foods worldwide.
PEP.bull: Cheaper than Coke at ~16x with a 4.5% yield; activist pressure is pushing cost cuts.
PEP.bear: Losing fountain accounts and snack volumes are weak.
PEP.take: Near its lows on share losses; a value case depends on the snack business turning.

PFE.name: Pfizer
PFE.about: Global drugmaker; owns the Prevnar pneumococcal vaccine franchise.
PFE.bear: Revenue shrinking and Prevnar faces Vaxcyte's broader vaccine later this decade.
PFE.take: Cheap income stock with a slowly growing competitive threat to a key franchise.

PLTR.name: Palantir
PLTR.about: Data and AI software for government and commercial clients.
PLTR.bull: Revenue +59% with 49% net margins; a tech-first Pentagon helps.
PLTR.bear: ~100x forward earnings and 74x sales; near the target already.

PNC.name: PNC Financial Services
PNC.bull: Q3 EPS beat ($5.09 vs $4.89); ~24% upside to target; 3.7% yield.
PNC.bear: Revenue slightly missed; loan growth is slow.
PNC.take: A steady regional bank at ~10x forward earnings after a clean beat.

PR.name: Permian Resources
PR.about: Pure-play Permian Basin oil and gas producer.
PR.bull: Cheap at ~10x forward earnings and ~5.5x EBITDA, with a 2.7% dividend; Scotiabank upgraded it Oct 16.
PR.bear: Already up ~90% in a year; a ceasefire or sanctions relief that cools oil would hit it.
PR.take: A lower-cost way to own $100+ oil with a solid balance sheet.

PYPD.name: PolyPid
PYPD.about: Israeli biotech whose lead drug D-PLEX100 is a local slow-release antibiotic to prevent infections after abdominal surgery.
PYPD.bull: Priority-review FDA decision on Nov 28 with Azurity already licensed (deal worth up to ~$320M); ~$97M market cap and a ~$11.75 average target.
PYPD.bear: Binary: a rejection would likely force a dilutive raise; shares more than doubled in a year; economics are mostly milestones and royalties.
PYPD.take: A small, partner-backed FDA bet; position sizing matters because a rejection could cut the price in half or worse.
PYPD.catalyst: FDA decision (PDUFA) on D-PLEX100 for preventing surgical-site infections after colorectal surgery; priority review
PYPD.runway: Only $6.6M cash at Jun 30, but the company says expected Azurity proceeds fund it into 2028; that depends on milestones.

QRVO.name: Qorvo
QRVO.about: RF chip maker for phones, defense and infrastructure; Apple is a large customer.
QRVO.bull: Defense and infrastructure segments diversify it more than Skyworks.
QRVO.bear: Trades above the average analyst target; Apple order cuts would hit it too.
QRVO.take: Delisted Oct 5, 2026 after merging into Skyworks (SWKS); last trade $114.17 on Oct 2.

RCAT.name: Red Cat Holdings
RCAT.about: Makes Black Widow reconnaissance drones for the US Army and allies.
RCAT.bull: Offered EUR 39/share (~$230M) for Austria's Steyr Motors (Oct 19) to own engines for its uncrewed boats; revenue is growing fast from drone programs.
RCAT.bear: Must book $114M+ in H2 to hit guidance; 24% short interest; stock down ~20% this year.
RCAT.take: Dropped from Moonshots Oct 9: drone stocks are falling even on good news and it burns ~$158M a year.
RCAT.catalyst: Q3 results: needs a big second half to hit $150–180M 2026 revenue guidance
RCAT.runway: ~$326M cash; burned ~$158M last year, so about two years without a raise.

RKLB.name: Rocket Lab
RKLB.about: Small launch (Electron), Neutron rocket and spacecraft components.
RKLB.bull: The main listed alternative to SpaceX; ~50% upside to target.
RKLB.bear: Neutron's first flight slipped to 2027 (stock -10.9% on Oct 15); still ~43x sales and unprofitable.
RKLB.take: The Neutron delay removes the near-term catalyst; the stock now trades on Electron and space-systems growth until 2027.

RKT.name: Rocket Companies
RKT.about: Largest US mortgage lender (Rocket Mortgage, plus Mr. Cooper servicing).
RKT.bull: Target ~50% above price; a drop in rates would unleash refinancing volume.
RKT.bear: High beta (2.2); higher-for-longer rates keep volumes depressed.
RKT.take: Leveraged bet on mortgage rates falling.

RTX.name: RTX
RTX.about: Aerospace and defense group made up of Raytheon missiles, Pratt & Whitney engines and Collins Aerospace systems.
RTX.bull: It holds the parallel SM-6 and AMRAAM multiyear missile deals, so the push to ramp missile output (like Boeing's PAC-3 seeker award) supports its backlog.
RTX.bear: At about 24x forward earnings with thin net margins, the stock already prices in strong defense demand.
RTX.take: A large, steady beneficiary of the missile ramp, though its size means any single contract moves the needle little.

SCCO.name: Southern Copper
SCCO.about: Low-cost copper miner in Peru and Mexico, controlled by Grupo Mexico.
SCCO.bull: Huge reserves and a 36% net margin at record copper prices.
SCCO.bear: At ~31x earnings it trades ~18% above the average target, with a Sell consensus.
SCCO.take: Quality copper exposure that's priced for perfection.

SCHW.name: Charles Schwab
SCHW.about: Runs a large US brokerage, bank and wealth-management business serving individual investors and independent advisers.
SCHW.bull: Fed minutes point to another hike and short rates are rising, which lets Schwab earn more on the cash clients leave in their accounts.
SCHW.bear: With the 10-year at 5.36%, clients may move more cash into higher-yielding money funds, and higher rates can mark down its bond holdings.
SCHW.take: One of the clearer winners from higher-for-longer rates, at about 13x forward earnings with 22% revenue growth.

SLGL.name: Sol-Gel Technologies
SLGL.src: Twelve Data (Oct 14 close); other stats StockAnalysis
SLGL.about: Israeli dermatology company developing a topical gel to prevent skin cancers in Gorlin syndrome, a rare genetic condition.
SLGL.bull: Insiders own ~60%, cash covers years of spending, and there are no approved drugs for this condition. Breakthrough and Orphan designations.
SLGL.bear: One trial decides it; a miss could cut the stock in half or worse. Small float means big swings.
SLGL.take: The rare small cap where insiders own most of it and there's no near-term need to raise money. That's what makes it stand out.
SLGL.catalyst: Phase 3 topline for SGT-610 (patidegib gel) in Gorlin syndrome
SLGL.runway: ~$48M cash vs ~$9M yearly burn: several years.

SNDK.name: Sandisk
SNDK.about: NAND flash and enterprise SSDs, spun out of Western Digital.
SNDK.bull: AI inference needs fast storage; forward P/E around 8.
SNDK.bear: Up ~15x from its 52-week low. NAND pricing can reverse quickly.
SNDK.take: Same cycle risk as Micron with more momentum and less history.

SPCX.name: SpaceX
SPCX.about: Launch, Starlink satellite internet and AI compute; IPO'd June 2026 at $135.
SPCX.bull: Revenue +120% YoY; Starlink and AI-compute contracts (incl. $40B+ with Anthropic).
SPCX.bear: ~100x sales and losing money; insider lockups expire through Dec 8.
SPCX.take: Priced on the future. Lockup expiries are the near-term supply risk.

STNE.name: StoneCo
STNE.about: Small-mid cap Brazilian payments and banking for small businesses.
STNE.bear: Brazil's high interest rates hurt funding costs and merchant demand.
STNE.take: Deep value if Brazil's rates come down.

SVRA.name: Savara
SVRA.about: Rare-disease biotech developing inhaled molgramostim (MOLBREEVI) for autoimmune PAP.
SVRA.bull: First-ever approved drug for autoimmune PAP would make it a commercial orphan-drug company; JPMorgan started at Overweight ($12) Oct 7, and 34% short float could fuel a squeeze on approval.
SVRA.bear: Pure binary: a rejection or another delay (the review was extended before) would likely mean a sharp drop and dilution; launch in a tiny market may be slow.
SVRA.take: A defined-date FDA bet with real short-squeeze fuel; the downside if rejected is large.
SVRA.catalyst: FDA decision on MOLBREEVI (inhaled molgramostim) for autoimmune PAP; UK decision Q4 2026, EU Q1 2027
SVRA.runway: About $175M cash vs ~$110M/yr burn gives roughly 1.5 years; up to ~$150M non-dilutive capital is tied to approval.

SWKS.name: Skyworks Solutions
SWKS.about: Radio-frequency chips for phones, heavily dependent on Apple.
SWKS.bull: Cheap on forward earnings (~14x) with a ~2.8% dividend.
SWKS.bear: Apple reportedly cut iPhone 18 Pro orders; 22% of float is sold short.
SWKS.take: A phone-cycle stock caught on the wrong side of AI pulling parts and memory away from consumer devices.

T.name: AT&T Inc.
T.about: Telecom company offering wireless, fiber broadband and business connectivity services.
T.take: Listed comparable for a private-markets idea; use its multiples to sanity-check private valuations.

TECK.name: Teck Resources
TECK.about: Canadian miner focused on copper and zinc, including the QB2 copper mine in Chile.
TECK.bull: With copper near $14,400/t and a strike at Antofagasta's Centinela mine tightening supply, Teck's Chilean copper output (QB2) gains from higher prices (inferred).
TECK.bear: The shares sit well above the average analyst target, and Chilean labor unrest could spread to its own operations.
TECK.take: A direct play on copper prices that has already run hard; analysts on average see less upside than the stock price implies.

TMUS.name: T-Mobile US
TMUS.about: US wireless carrier that has led industry subscriber growth.
TMUS.bull: Best growth of the big three; analyst target far above the price.
TMUS.bear: Down ~34% in a year and -9.5% on the SpaceX spectrum deal.
TMUS.take: The market is repricing the whole carrier group for a Starlink-backed disruptor.

TNK.name: Teekay Tankers
TNK.about: Mid-size crude tankers; small-mid cap with a net-cash balance sheet.
TNK.bull: 1.5x book and ~5x EV/EBITDA even at elevated rates.
TNK.bear: Above analyst target; revenue already falling YoY.
TNK.take: Cheapest tanker on book value; most exposed to a reopening.

TSLA.name: Tesla
TSLA.about: Tesla designs, makes and sells electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems.
TSLA.bull: Energy storage, robotaxi and the new Roadster keep the long-term story alive.
TSLA.bear: Trades at ~180x forward earnings with low margins; the car business is slowing.
TSLA.take: Valued on autonomy hopes more than car sales; reports Oct 21.

TSM.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC)
TSM.about: The world's dominant contract chipmaker; builds nearly every leading AI processor.
TSM.bull: September sales +54.6% y/y; ~50% net margins and a target ~28% above the price.
TSM.bear: Taiwan geopolitical risk and US tariff threats; capex keeps rising.
TSM.take: The toll road of the AI build-out; monthly sales are the best real-time demand check.

UMAC.name: Unusual Machines
UMAC.about: Florida maker of US-built drone motors, cameras and components, plus an FPV drone retail business.
UMAC.bull: Policy tailwinds for non-Chinese drone parts; ~$316M cash and almost no debt; $39 average target.
UMAC.bear: ~33x sales on $32M revenue, still losing money, share count +182% in a year; 19% short and conflict-of-interest headlines around the Pentagon loan talks.
UMAC.take: A cash-rich, policy-driven small cap; the price already assumes a lot of growth.
UMAC.catalyst: Q3 results and any decision on a reported $220M Office of Strategic Capital loan
UMAC.runway: About $316M cash against ~$61M yearly burn is roughly 5 years of runway, built through repeated stock sales.

USAR.name: USA Rare Earth
USAR.about: Building a rare-earth magnet plant in Oklahoma; essentially pre-revenue.
USAR.bull: Target ~2.6x price if magnet production ramps.
USAR.take: Speculative small cap on US supply-chain policy.

USB.name: U.S. Bancorp
USB.bull: Record Q3 revenue ($7.97B); ~10x forward earnings and a 3.8% yield.
USB.bear: Rate-sensitive deposits and credit costs if growth slows.
USB.take: A cheap, steady regional bank after a clean quarter.

UTHR.name: United Therapeutics
UTHR.about: Develops and sells treatments for pulmonary arterial hypertension and other serious lung diseases.
UTHR.bull: It already runs a profitable inhaled rare-lung franchise with 40%+ net margins, and has the cash flow to be a buyer of companies like Savara.
UTHR.bear: A new rare-lung-disease drug like Savara's, up for FDA approval Nov 22, adds competition for specialist attention in its core market.
UTHR.take: A profitable, low-beta rare-lung leader at about 20x earnings; the Savara decision mainly matters as a sign of where the space and deal activity are heading.

VAL.name: Valaris
VAL.about: Large offshore driller with floaters and jackups.
VAL.bull: Low P/E (6.4x) on one-off gains; strong deepwater day rates.
VAL.take: A larger, less leveraged offshore peer to Borr.

VLO.name: Valero
VLO.bull: 8x forward earnings; cheaper crude with tight fuel supply widens margins.
VLO.bear: Trades ~16% above the average analyst target after a big run.
VLO.take: Strong earnings but the stock is ahead of the analysts.

VNDA.name: Vanda Pharmaceuticals
VNDA.about: Commercial-stage CNS and immunology drugmaker (Fanapt, HETLIOZ, PONVORY, newly approved BYSANTI and NEREUS) with a BLA for imsidolimab (Quimilza) in generalized pustular psoriasis under FDA review.
VNDA.bull: A Quimilza approval plus BYSANTI launch traction could re-rate a stock that trades near 1.3x sales and book value. Fanapt grew 23% YoY in Q2.
VNDA.bear: VQW-765 failed its Phase 3 in social anxiety (Oct 14) and that program is paused; cash burn is heavy, and a Dec 12 rejection would leave little else near term. Shares sit at a 52-week low.
VNDA.take: Cash covers most of the market cap, so you pay little for the pipeline. The launch and the Dec 12 decision decide whether the burn slows.
VNDA.catalyst: FDA decision on Quimilza (imsidolimab) for generalized pustular psoriasis
VNDA.runway: The company says its $170M cash (Jun 30, 2026) funds operations through at least the end of 2027.

VRT.name: Vertiv
VRT.about: Power and liquid-cooling systems for data centers.
VRT.bull: Hotter AI racks require liquid cooling; analysts see ~34% upside.
VRT.bear: Off 34% from its high; growth (24%) is slower than chip names.
VRT.take: PEG under 1. A picks-and-shovels play that doesn't depend on which chip wins.

VTRS.name: Viatris
VTRS.about: Generic and branded drugmaker; partner on Opus Genetics' presbyopia eye drop.
VTRS.bull: Buying Pacira for $1.65B adds cash-producing non-opioid pain drugs; also partners Opus on the Oct 17 presbyopia decision.
VTRS.bear: Low growth and a net loss over the last year.
VTRS.take: Turning a generics giant into a branded-drug company, one deal at a time.

VZ.name: Verizon
VZ.about: Largest US wireless carrier by revenue.
VZ.bull: ~8x forward earnings with a ~6.8% dividend; target ~23% higher.
VZ.bear: SpaceX buying spectrum threatens a new price war; -8.7% on Oct 9.
VZ.take: A high-yield value stock whose risk just changed from slow growth to a new competitor.

WMT.name: Walmart
WMT.about: Largest retailer; wins when shoppers trade down.
WMT.bull: Gains share from squeezed middle-income shoppers; ad and membership income growing.
WMT.bear: 35x forward for a grocer is rich.
WMT.take: Defensive, but you pay a premium for the safety.

WOLF.name: Wolfspeed
WOLF.about: Wolfspeed makes silicon carbide materials and power devices for power electronics and RF applications.
WOLF.bull: Post-restructuring silicon-carbide maker winning 200mm wafer deals as data-center power demand grows.
WOLF.bear: Revenue still shrinking (-12%), huge short interest, and a history of cash burn and dilution.
WOLF.take: A high-risk turnaround; supply deals help, but shares swing hard on any news.

XP.name: XP Inc.
XP.about: Brazil's largest independent brokerage and investment platform.
XP.bull: Most leveraged to Brazilian market sentiment and trading volumes.
XP.take: High-beta Brazil play. Moves on the runoff odds.
